#### Run 17z9b: Gutmorn, Duelists' Convocation International and The Fourth Doctor write their trigger conditions; the discard and land-play defaults record the event

Row 17z9b, in one run, not split. The four sites: `DiscardTriggerCollectorService.handleGutmornOnDiscard`,
`SpellCastTriggerCollectorService.handleDuelistsConvocationInternational` (both watches, cast and land play), and The
Fourth Doctor's `handleFoodWhenCastingFromLibraryTop` and `PlayedCardNameTriggerCollectorService.handleFoodWhenPlayingLandFromLibraryTop`.
Each judged a trigger condition by the effect's class and bound or baked event data. All four are gone.

**When the value is read.**

- Gutmorn, Pactbound Servant ("whenever a player discards a card during your turn, they choose another player …"):
  "during your turn" is the ability's event condition (`ControllerTurn`), judged only as the card is discarded (CR 603.2,
  checked), as the handler judged it. "They" and "that card" are the discarding player and the card as discarded, which
  the discard default records on the entry (`triggeringPlayerId`, `setTriggeringCards`); the card is a frozen card
  object, so the duplicate is of the card as it was discarded even after it has left the graveyard, as the handler's
  snapshot was. The handler's non-targeting `targetId` and `discardedCardSnapshot` are not used any more.
- Duelists' Convocation International ("whenever you play a land or cast a spell, if it shares a mana value with one or
  more uncrossed digits …"): the intervening "if" (CR 603.4, checked) is the ability's option,
  `TriggeringCardManaValueIsUncrossedChosenDigit`, judged as the spell is cast or the land played and again as the
  ability resolves (the `ConditionalEffect` the readers wrap). "It" is the triggering spell as it is on the stack, X the
  number chosen for it (CR 202.3e, checked) and 0 cast face down, else the land played. The effect reads the same from
  the entry (the triggering spell's snapshot, else the triggering card), no longer the baked event value; the handler's
  resolution check was the same.
- The Fourth Doctor ("once each turn, you may play a historic land or cast a historic spell from the top of your library.
  When you do, create a Food token"): the zone and the historic filter are the triggers' (`castFrom(Zone.LIBRARY)`,
  `playedFrom(Zone.LIBRARY)`, `withFilter(historic)`), judged on the spell as cast and the land as played as the
  handlers did; "when you do" is the event condition `SourceLibraryPlayPermissionUsedThisTurn` (the source's
  once-each-turn permission is marked used before the cast and land-play triggers are collected), with the ability's
  `TriggerLimit.ONCE_EACH_TURN` as before. The two together are the handlers' check: the permission is used once each
  turn, and the Food ability triggers on that use.

**May timing.** No "you may" moved; none of the three abilities has one.

**Rules fix.** "Whenever you discard a card" abilities' options weren't judged as the ability triggers:
`TriggerCollectionService.collectControllerDiscardAbilities` dispatched the effects with the intervening "if" wrapped
around them (checked only as the ability resolved) and ignored an event condition. It now judges both through the watch
judge, as the opponent-discard reader already did. Cool but Rude's level 2 ability ("whenever you discard a card, this
Class deals 2 damage to each opponent") is written as an intervening "if" on the Class level, which the Class has only at
level 2 or greater (CR 716.2a, checked); below that a discard put the ability on the stack, where it did nothing. The new
case `CoolButRudeTest#levelOneDiscardDoesNotTriggerTheLevelTwoAbility` fails at HEAD (the ability is on the stack).
Gutmorn's own-discard half needs the event condition judged there.

Two new Duelists' Convocation International cases guard what moved and pass at HEAD too:
`#adventureSpellUsesTheAdventuresManaValue` (Stomp has only the Adventure's characteristics on the stack, CR 715.3b,
checked: mana value 2) and `#digitCrossedOutBeforeResolutionStopsTheAbility` (two Shocks: the second's trigger crosses the
only 1 first, and the first's then does nothing).

Rulings (checked with `get_rulings`): Gutmorn, Pactbound Servant has none; The Fourth Doctor's are about Food and looking
at the top card; Duelists' Convocation International (a playtest card) has no Scryfall entry, its Oracle text read from
the MTGJSON card data; Cool but Rude's Oracle text read with `get_card`. The abilities agree with each.

**The model.**

- New conditions `TriggeringCardManaValueIsUncrossedChosenDigit` and `SourceLibraryPlayPermissionUsedThisTurn`, judged in
  `ConditionEvaluationService`; `Permanent.uncrossedChosenNumberDigitPosition(int)`, read by the condition and the
  effect handler.
- `CreateFoodWhenPlayingCardFromTopOfLibraryEffect` is gone.
- `DiscardTriggerCollectorService.handleDiscardDefault` is the default of both "you discard" and "an opponent discards"
  (there was no opponent default: an untargeted effect with no handler of its own didn't trigger); its entry records the
  discarding player as the triggering player and the card discarded as the triggering card.
- `PlayedCardNameTriggerCollectorService`: the land-play defaults record the land played as the triggering card (its id
  and `triggeringCards`), as the filtered collector already did; `collectLandPlayAbility` judges the event condition
  (it ignored one) and gives both options the land as the triggering card.
- `TriggerCollectionService.collectUnfilteredAbility` gives a land-play ability's options the land played as the
  triggering card; `collectControllerDiscardAbilities` judges the abilities' options (the rules fix).
- `EffectResolutionService`'s resolution-time triggering card for a condition that reads it (now also
  `TriggeringCardManaValueIsUncrossedChosenDigit`) falls back to the entry's triggering spell or card when the entry has
  no triggering card id.
- `DuelistsConvocationInternationalTriggerEffectHandler` inserts its draw (and win) after the resolving effect's index,
  as the effect is now wrapped in the intervening "if"'s `ConditionalEffect`.

**Cards (by script).** `scripts/step15-run17z9b-cards.py` (idempotent, per letter module):

- Gutmorn, Pactbound Servant: one ability, `addTrigger(List.of(Triggers.youDiscardCard(),
  Triggers.opponentDiscardsCard()), TriggerOptions.DEFAULT.withEventCondition(new ControllerTurn()), effect)`.
- Duelists' Convocation International: one ability, `addTrigger(List.of(Triggers.youPlayLand(),
  Triggers.youCastSpell().anySpell()), TriggerOptions.DEFAULT.withInterveningIf(new
  TriggeringCardManaValueIsUncrossedChosenDigit()), new DuelistsConvocationInternationalTriggerEffect())`.
- The Fourth Doctor: `addTrigger(List.of(Triggers.youCastSpell().withFilter(historic).castFrom(Zone.LIBRARY),
  Triggers.youPlayLand().withFilter(historic).playedFrom(Zone.LIBRARY)), TriggerOptions.DEFAULT.withLimit(
  TriggerLimit.ONCE_EACH_TURN).withEventCondition(new SourceLibraryPlayPermissionUsedThisTurn()),
  CreateTokenEffect.ofFoodToken(1))`.

**Behaviour changes.**

- The rules fix above.
- The untargeted "whenever you discard a card" default entries now record the discarding player and the card; the
  unfiltered land-play entries record the land played (its id and as a triggering card). No converted reader is
  affected (the discard, land-play and triggering-card cards' classes pass).
- `TriggeringCardMatches` judged as an ability resolves now sees the entry's triggering spell or card when the entry has
  no triggering card id (before, it saw none and was false).
- Otherwise none intended.

For step 16: no new `Card`, `StackEntry` or `GameData` state, one `Permanent` method; four class-keyed handlers and one
record gone; nothing new is slot-keyed.

#### Run 17z11: the named class-keyed bindings and the multiplayer "opponent" picks read the event; the services the audit missed are classified

Row 17z11, split into 17z11 and 17z11b to 17z11f. Measured with the new `scripts/step15-run17z11-audit.py` (below),
which reads every effect-class read in the combat, step, enter and trigger-collection services: 419 reads, of which 148
still bind event data, rebuild or unwrap a card's effect by its class (and one `getOpponentId` pick), in five families,
each a run of its own (rows 17z11b to 17z11f). This run did the row's named bindings, the three `getOpponentId` picks
it named and a fourth the audit found (Zidane, Tantalus Thief).

The sites:

- `CombatAttackService`'s self-attack collector: `OtherAttackingCreatureReferenceEffect` (a marker interface) made the
  other declared attacker the "you may" ability's non-targeting `targetId` (Creepy Puppeteer);
  `GameData.queueGrantedMayAbility` and `MayAbilityHandlerService` set `nonTargeting` by the same class.
- `CombatAttackService`'s "a creature you control attacks" collector: a "you may" wrapping a
  `DealDamageToTargetPlayerOrPlaneswalkerEffect` got the attacking creature as its target choice's source permanent
  (Rage Forger's "have that creature deal 1 damage").
- `CombatDamageService`: a "you may" wrapping `SacrificeSelfAndTargetDiscardsPerPoisonCounterEffect` had an entry of its
  own with the defending player as `targetId` (Whispering Specter).
- `TriggerCollectionService.queueNoncombatDamageToPlayerEffect`: the event value went on a "you may" entry only when it
  wrapped a `DrawCardEffect` with an `EventValue` amount, and on a plain entry only for a `DiscardEffect`, or a
  `DrawCardEffect` or `MillEffect` with an `EventValue`.
- `PermanentChoiceTriggerHandlerService.handleDeathTrigger`: a `DealDamageToTargetPlayerOrPlaneswalkerEffect` with
  `triggeringCreatureDealsDamage` made the dying card the entry's damage source card (Stalking Vengeance): the same
  "that creature deals" as Rage Forger's, so it moved with it.
- The picks: `LandTapTriggerCollectorService.handleCreateTokenForOpponentOnSelfTapped` (Forbidden Orchard's "target
  opponent", `getOpponentId`'s one with no choice), `ManaTapTriggerCollectorService.handleGainControlOfOpponentArtifact`
  (Treasure Nabber's "an opponent", judged as `getOpponentId`'s one), `MiscTriggerCollectorService.handleCoinFlipLostDefault`
  (Karplusan Minotaur's "any target of an opponent's choice", chosen by `getOpponentId`'s one) and
  `TriggerCollectionService.checkOpponentGainsControlTriggers` (Zidane's "whenever an opponent gains control of a
  permanent from you", only for `getOpponentId`'s one).

**When the value is read.**

- Creepy Puppeteer ("you may have that creature's base power and toughness become 4/3"): "that creature" is the one
  other creature declared as an attacker with it. The self-attack collector records the declared attackers on every
  untargeted "you may" entry as its attacking creatures (`StackEntry.attackingPermanentSnapshots`, as the "you attack"
  entries do), whatever the effect; the effect reads the one other than the source as the ability resolves and changes
  it wherever it is on the battlefield. The collector picked the same creature as the ability triggered. The
  intervening "if" (`ExactlyAttackers(2)`) is unchanged, judged as it triggers and again as it resolves (CR 603.4).
- Rage Forger and Stalking Vengeance ("that creature" / "it deals damage"): the creature the trigger event was about,
  the entry's triggering permanent (the attacking creature, which the attack target choice already recorded; the dying
  creature, which the death target choice already recorded), deals the damage as it is or as it last existed (CR
  608.2h, checked): `DealDamageToTargetPlayerOrPlaneswalkerEffect.byTriggeringCreature` deals it through
  `DamageSupport.entryDealtByTriggeringPermanent`, as `DealDamageToPlayersEffect.dealtByTriggeringPermanent()` does.
  Rage Forger's target choice has Rage Forger as its source permanent, as every other targeted ability of the collector
  does. The ally-death target choice records the dying creature's controller as the triggering permanent's controller,
  which is the departed creature's damage controller (its lifelink's).
- Whispering Specter ("that player discards a card for each poison counter they have"): "that player" is the player
  dealt damage, which the combat damage collector's generic "you may" path records as the entry's triggering player
  (and non-targeting `targetId`); the effect reads the triggering player. The sacrifice and the count are as the
  ability resolves, as before.
- A noncombat damage-to-a-player ability's entry records the damage dealt as its event value and the player dealt it as
  its triggering player whatever its effects are, as the combat damage collector already did.
- Forbidden Orchard ("target opponent creates a token"): the ability targets, so it is no mana ability (CR 605.1b,
  checked) and its target is chosen as it goes on the stack (CR 603.3d, checked); the effect is
  `CreateTokenForTargetPlayerEffect(…, PlayerRelation.OPPONENT)`, and the choice offers the players the relation allows.
- Treasure Nabber ("whenever an opponent taps an artifact for mana") and Zidane ("whenever an opponent gains control of
  a permanent from you"): in a game of individuals every other player is an opponent (CR 806.1, checked). Treasure
  Nabber's entry also records the tapping player and the tapped artifact as its triggering player and permanent.
- Karplusan Minotaur ("deals 1 damage to any target of an opponent's choice"): as the ability goes on the stack its
  controller chooses one of their opponents, who chooses the target (CR 801.5b's example has the controller choose the
  opponent who makes "an opponent chooses" choice; checked); with one opponent there's no question. The new
  `SpellTargetTriggerAnyTarget.chosenByAnOpponent()` marks the choice, and the target-choice drain asks the controller
  first (`PermanentChoiceContext.ChooseOpponentToChooseTriggerTarget`). The coin-flip-lost default still gives every
  "whenever you lose a coin flip" ability a target of an opponent's choice; Karplusan Minotaur is the only such card.

**May timing.** No "you may" moved: Creepy Puppeteer's, Rage Forger's and Whispering Specter's are asked as the
ability resolves (CR 603.5, checked), as before.

**Rules fixes.**

- **"Target opponent" is chosen** (Forbidden Orchard): in a game with more than one opponent the collector gave the
  token to one without a choice. The new `ForbiddenOrchardTest#controllerChoosesWhichOpponentCreatesTheSpirit` offers
  both opponents and not the controller in a three-player game, and gives the token to the one chosen.
- **"An opponent" is any opponent** (Treasure Nabber, Zidane): the abilities triggered only for the player
  `getOpponentId` named. The new `TreasureNabberTest#triggersWhenAnyOpponentTapsAnArtifactForMana` and
  `ZidaneTantalusThiefTest#anyOpponentGainingControlCreatesTreasure` use the third player.
- **"Of an opponent's choice" lets the controller choose the opponent** (Karplusan Minotaur): the new
  `KarplusanMinotaurTest#lostFlipControllerChoosesTheOpponentWhoChoosesTheTarget` (three players; the loss's triggers
  collected directly through the trigger collection service, a coin flip being random) has the controller choose the
  third player, who chooses the target.

All four fail at HEAD (below).

Rulings (checked with `get_rulings`): Creepy Puppeteer, Rage Forger and Forbidden Orchard have none; Whispering Specter
(the sacrifice and the poison count are as it resolves), Treasure Nabber (an artifact is tapped for mana by activating
its {T} mana ability; with several Nabbers the artifact moves in turn), Karplusan Minotaur (the triggers wait until the
flips are done, each may have a different target), Zidane (a Treasure for each permanent). The abilities agree with each.

#### Run 17z11b: the damage-to-a-player collectors record the event whatever the effects are; `CombatDamageTriggerContextEffect` is gone

Row 17z11b, in one run, not split. `CombatDamageTriggerContextEffect` was a capability interface (124 implementers in
`model/effect/`, the wrappers `MayEffect`, `MayPayManaEffect`, `ConditionalEffect`, `SequenceEffect`, `ChooseOneEffect`,
`QueueReflexiveAbilityEffect` and the sacrifice- and counter-then wrappers forwarding their payload's) by which an effect
told the damage collectors what to put on its entry: `DAMAGED_PLAYER` (the damaged player as `targetId`, and a player
target spec not chosen), `SOURCE_SELF` (the dealing creature as source), `DAMAGED_PLAYER_WITH_DAMAGE_AMOUNT` (the damage
as `xValue`), `CHOSEN_PLAYER` (the source's remembered player as `targetId`) and `ENCHANTED_CREATURE_CONTROLLER`. Before
changing anything a temporary probe (removed before the run ended) logged every read, with the effect's context, target
kinds and whether the card declares a target for it, over the test classes of every card with a damage-to-a-player
trigger, a modal or a reflexive ability (1,946 classes, all passing at HEAD).

The sites:

- `CombatDamageService`'s own reader: the context chose the entry's `targetId`, `xValue` and source, and a non-null
  context suppressed the choice of a player target the effect's spec declared.
- Its attached reader (an Aura's or Equipment's "enchanted / equipped creature deals combat damage to a player"):
  `ENCHANTED_CREATURE_CONTROLLER` or a `CreateTokenForTriggeringPlayerEffect` made the creature's controller the
  `targetId`; `SOURCE_SELF` or `DAMAGED_PLAYER` made the creature, not the Aura or Equipment, the entry's source, unless
  a `DealDamageToPlayersEffect` was among the effects.
- Its curse reader: only effects reporting `SOURCE_SELF` or `DAMAGED_PLAYER` triggered at all, `SOURCE_SELF` with the
  creature as source (Curse of Stalked Prey).
- Its ally reader: `CHOSEN_PLAYER` made the remembered player the `targetId` (Saskia); a second target-choice branch
  keyed by the context was unreachable.
- Its dealt-damage reader and `DamageTriggerCollectorService`'s: `DealDamageToPlayersEffect(CHOSEN_PLAYER)` bound the
  remembered player (Stuffy Doll); `DamageTriggerCollectorService`'s equipped reader: `DAMAGED_PLAYER` set the
  `targetId`.
- `TriggerCollectionService.queueNoncombatDamageToPlayerEffect`: the context chose `targetId`, source and `xValue`.
- `TriggeredAbilityQueueService.queueChosenTriggeredModalTrigger`, `StackedModalTriggerService.usesBoundDamagedPlayer`,
  `ChoiceHandlerService.beginResolvingModalTargetChoice`: the modal's `DAMAGED_PLAYER` bound a mode's player to the
  trigger's; `QueueReflexiveAbilityEffectHandler`, `RemoveCounterFromSourceThenEffectHandler`: the reflexive effect's.
- `CombatTriggerService`: a `CreateTokenForTriggeringPlayerEffect` made an Aura's own attack trigger an ability of the
  enchanted creature (Invocation of Saint Traft); an `EquippedCreatureDealsDamageToDefendingPlayerEffect` recorded the
  creature's card and controller in the auto-targeted and per-blocker paths (Simian Sling, Tormentor's Helm).

What the probe found: on the creature's own reader every player-target effect with a context was "that player" and every
one without a context had a target the card declares (`target(...)`: Heist, a `MillEffect`, a
`DrawCardForTargetPlayerEffect`); the ally and noncombat readers never chose an undeclared player target; the modal and
reflexive sites met only "that player" effects. So "that player" is exactly a player target the card doesn't declare,
the rule the ally reader already applied, and no effect needs to say so.

**When the value is read.**

- Every damage-to-a-player collector records the event the same way whatever the effects are: the player dealt damage as
  the entry's triggering player and, when no target is chosen, its non-targeting `targetId` (the cast and land-play
  collectors' convention since run 17z9), the damage as its event value. The `TARGET_PLAYER` / `TRIGGERING_PLAYER`
  recipients and the "that player" effects read the `targetId` as the ability resolves, as before. A player target the
  card declares is chosen as the ability goes on the stack (CR 603.3d, checked); one it doesn't declare is "that
  player", no target (CR 115.10a, checked).
- "That many" (Balefire Dragon, Shockmaw Dragon, Cephalid Constable and the granted creature bounce, Gishath's "reveal
  that many cards") is the entry's event value as the ability resolves; nothing is baked into `xValue`.
  `LookAtTopXCardsPermanentsToBattlefieldRestToGraveyardEffect` gained a `count` amount (`XValue`, the spells' X, by
  default; `EventValue` for Gishath).
- An Aura's, Equipment's or Curse's ability keeps the Aura, Equipment or Curse as its source (CR 113.7, checked) and
  records the creature that dealt the damage as its triggering permanent (id, controller, last-known snapshot) and event
  damage source; "it" / "that creature" read it as the ability resolves: Curse of Stalked Prey's counter
  (`PutCounterOnReferencedPermanentEffect(TRIGGERING)`), Mask of the Schemer's "it connives X"
  (`DrawDiscardAndConniveEffect.ofTriggeringPermanent(EventValue)`, its last-known information the triggering snapshot),
  Ogre-Head Helm's "you may sacrifice it" (`SacrificeSelfThenEffect.ofTriggeringPermanent`: the triggering permanent when
  the entry records one, else the source, as the ruling says; `MayEffectHandler`'s can-sacrifice check reads the same
  permanent), Semblance Scanner's "a duplicate of it" and Super State's "it deals that much damage" (the triggering
  permanent, else its snapshot), Celestial Mantle's "its controller" (the enchanted creature's controller as it
  resolves, else the triggering permanent's). `EnchantedPermanentMatches` judged with a triggering permanent that has
  left reads the creature the Aura is attached to now (Breath of Fury's "if it's attached to a creature" after moving).
- "The chosen player" (`DealDamageToPlayersEffect(CHOSEN_PLAYER)`) is read from the source permanent's remembered player,
  or its last-known information, as the ability resolves (Saskia, Stuffy Doll, Black Vise); a spell's (Backdraft) is the
  `targetId` its earlier effect chose. The choice can't change, so it is the player the collectors bound.
- A triggered modal whose chosen modes target nothing has the attacked or damaged player as its non-targeting
  `targetId`. A mode chosen as the ability goes on the stack or as it resolves whose effects have no permanent target
  and no player target the card declares reuses the entry's player, as does a reflexive "when you do" ability
  (`QueueReflexiveAbilityEffect`, `RemoveCounterFromSourceThenEffect`), which also carries the entry's triggering player;
  an untargeted reflexive ability carries the entry's player as its non-targeting `targetId`.
- Invocation of Saint Traft and Sticky Fingers grant their abilities ("enchanted creature has '…'",
  `GrantTriggeredAbilityEffect`): the creature is the source and its controller controls the ability (CR 113.7, 113.8,
  checked), as the attack collector's class check did for Invocation and the attached reader's `targetId` did for
  Sticky Fingers' token.
- The auto-targeted and per-blocker attached attack and block collectors record the creature's controller and
  last-known snapshot whatever the effects are, as their untargeted path already did.
- `CastCardFromGraveyardEffectHandler` reads its `targetId` as a chosen card only when it isn't a player (Sword of Once
  and Future's equipped entry now carries the damaged player).

**May timing.** No "you may" moved: each is asked as the ability resolves (CR 603.5, checked), as before; Ogre-Head
Helm's is withheld, as before, when the creature to sacrifice is another player's.

**Rules fixes.**

- **A combat damage modal's "that player" isn't targeted** (Blizzard Specter, and every triggered modal whose chosen
  modes target nothing): its entry had the damaged player as `targetId` without being non-targeting, so it was checked as
  a target as it resolved and a player with hexproof (CR 702.11c, checked) made the ability do nothing. The new

Rulings (checked with `get_rulings`): Ogre-Head Helm (the equipped creature is sacrificed), Mask of the Schemer (a
creature that left still connives), Invocation of Saint Traft (the token's attacked player is chosen; removing the Aura
doesn't stop the delayed exile), Curse of Stalked Prey (any creature dealing combat damage to the enchanted player),
Sticky Fingers (none). The abilities agree with each.

EventValue())`), Curse of Stalked Prey (`PutCounterOnReferencedPermanentEffect(TRIGGERING, PLUS_ONE_PLUS_ONE)`), Mask of

#### Run 17z11c: the block collectors record "that creature" whatever the effects are; `CombatOpponentReferencingEffect` is gone

Row 17z11c, split into 17z11c and 17z11c2; row 17z11d was not started in this run and stays open as
written). `CombatOpponentReferencingEffect` was a capability interface (23 implementers in `model/effect/` plus
`MayEffect` and `SequenceEffect` forwarding their payload's, and three scope-keyed overrides: `GrantKeywordEffect`,
`RemoveKeywordEffect` and `SkipNextUntapEffect` with a `TARGET` scope, `TapPermanentsEffect` with
`TARGET_PLAYERS_PERMANENTS`, `PutCardToBattlefieldEffect` entering blocking) by which an effect told the combat
collectors to give it the creature on the other side of the block as its non-targeting `targetId`. Before changing
anything a temporary probe (removed before the run ended) logged every read of it and of the block collectors' class
lists, with the effect's target kinds and whether its card declares a target for it (`Card.hasEffectTargetIndex`), over
the test classes of every card with a block, "becomes blocked" or combat damage trigger, a combat-opponent effect or a
block-gate record (1,280 classes, all passing at HEAD).

The sites:

- `CombatBlockService`'s block collector and its effect-made-block twin (`collectEffectBlockTrigger`): a nine-class
  `needsAttackerTarget` list (`DestroyBlockedCreatureAndSelfEffect`, `DestroyTargetPermanentThenEffect`,
  `SkipNextUntapEffect(TARGET)`, `DealDamageToTargetCreatureEffect`, `DestroyCombatOpponentAtEndOfCombatEffect`, the
  interface, `PutCounterOnCombatOpponentAtEndOfCombatEffect`, `DestroyEquipmentOnEquipped…`, `GrantKeywordEffect(TARGET)`)
  chose the blocked attacker or the blocker itself as `targetId`; a card-level target filter
  (`Card.getTargetFilter() != null`) chose a target choice instead.
- The same collectors and the "becomes blocked" collectors (`fireCreatureBecomesBlockedTriggers`,
  `collectEffectBecomesBlockedTriggers`, `fireBecomesBlockedTriggersWithoutBlockers`): gates and rebuilds by class:
  `BoostSelfWhenBlockingKeywordEffect` (rebuilt as `BoostSelfEffect` when the attacker had the keyword),
  `BoostSelfWhenCombatOpponentMatchesEffect` (rebuilt as `BoostSelfEffect` plus `GrantKeywordEffect(SELF)` when an
  opponent matched), `DestroyEquipmentOnEquippedCombatOpponentAtEndOfCombatEffect` (dropped unless the opponent had
  Equipment) and `DestroyCombatOpponentAtEndOfCombatEffect` (dropped unless its filter matched); a granted, unfiltered
  "becomes blocked" ability was "becomes blocked by a creature" (once per blocker) when its effect was a
  combat-opponent effect, else once.
- `CombatTriggerService`'s Aura and Equipment readers (`checkAuraTriggersForCreature` for blocks,
  `checkAttachedPerBlockerTriggers`): a combat-opponent effect got the opponent as `targetId` (and
  `DestroyCombatOpponentAtEndOfCombatEffect`'s filter gated it); any other permanent or player target was chosen.
- `CombatDamageService`'s own and ally damage-to-a-player readers: a combat-opponent effect was never given a target
  choice.

What the probe found: on every block, "becomes blocked by a creature" and attached block ability that met one, every
effect with a permanent target spec that its card doesn't declare a target for was given the combat opponent, and every
declared one (Elite Javelineer, Goblin Javelineer, Rust Scarab, Merfolk Skyscout, Getaway Car, Clockwork Hydra, Laccolith
Rig, Super-Soldier Serum) was chosen; the two with no permanent target spec that the list gave the attacker
(`ReturnCombatOpponentToHandAtEndOfCombatEffect`, `CreateTokenBlockingCombatOpponentEffect`) read it too; the effects
the list gave the blocker itself read their source, not `targetId`. The damage readers met one combat-opponent effect
(Nature's Will's sequence, whose player target the card doesn't declare, so "that player" either way); no granted
"becomes blocked" ability met in the tests had a combat-opponent effect. So "that creature" is exactly a permanent target
the card doesn't declare, the rule run 17z11b found for "that player", and no effect needs to say so. The regular
(once) "becomes blocked" abilities name no single creature, and keep choosing any target their effects take (Karplusan
Wolverine, the Laccoliths), as before.

**When the value is read.**

- Every block and "becomes blocked by a creature" collector records the creature on the other side of the block the same
  way whatever the effects are (`CombatBlockService.recordCombatOpponent`): as the entry's triggering permanent (id,
  controller, a last-known copy) and non-targeting `targetId`, with its power and toughness as the ability triggered. A
  permanent or player target the card declares is chosen as the ability goes on the stack (CR 603.3d, checked); one it
  doesn't declare is that creature, which is no target (CR 115.10a, checked), so the ability can't fizzle. The effects
  read `targetId` (or the triggering permanent) as they resolve, as before; effects of the blocker itself read their
  source.
- An Aura's or Equipment's block ability keeps the enchanted or equipped creature as its triggering permanent (run
  17z11b) and records the other creature as its non-targeting `targetId`, now for every such entry (before: only for a
  combat-opponent effect, `null` otherwise); its per-blocker "becomes blocked by a creature" entries record the blocker
  the same way.
- A "[filter] creature" is the trigger's filter (`Triggers.blocks().withFilter`, `Triggers.becomesBlocked().withFilter`),
  judged as the creature blocks or becomes blocked (CR 509.3f, checked): "blocks a [filter] creature" on the creature it
  blocks (CR 509.3b), "blocks one or more [filter] creatures" (`ONE_OR_MORE`) on any creature it blocks (CR 509.3a),
  "becomes blocked by a [filter] creature" (`EACH_BLOCKER`) for each blocker that matches (CR 509.3d), and "becomes
  blocked by one or more [filter] creatures" (no `EACH_BLOCKER`, which the collector threw on before) once if any blocker
  matches (CR 509.3c); all checked. The gates the records carried were judged at the same moment, so the cards trigger
  as before.
- A granted "becomes blocked" ability is "becomes blocked by a creature" when it says so (`EACH_BLOCKER`) or has a filter
  on the blocker, as the printed ones; nothing judges its effect's class.
- An attacker made blocked by an effect's blocker (`applyBlockFromEffect`: Balduvian Warlord, the blocking swaps) goes
  through the same "becomes blocked" collector as a declared block, so its delayed "becomes blocked" abilities trigger
  too (CR 509.3c, checked), which they didn't (below).

**May timing.** No "you may" moved: each is asked as the ability resolves (CR 603.5, checked), as before.

**Rules fixes.**

- **A creature made blocked by an effect gets its delayed "becomes blocked" abilities** (Balduvian Warlord's reassigned
  blocker and Barreling Attack's "when that creature becomes blocked this turn"): the effect-made block collector never
  read the delayed abilities. The new `BalduvianWarlordTest#reassignedBlockerTriggersDelayedBecomesBlockedAbility` has
  the reassigned blocker block an unblocked creature Barreling Attack targeted; it fails at HEAD (below). A first
  version of the case used Lazotep Sliver's continuously granted afflict, which HEAD already triggered, and was replaced.

Rulings (checked with `get_rulings`): Corrosive Ooze (the Equipment is determined as the delayed ability resolves,
last-known if the creature left; unchanged), Crimson Roc, Woolly Spider, Dwarven Soldier and the Basilisks (none or
nothing on the trigger). The abilities agree with each.

**The model.**

- Gone: `CombatOpponentReferencingEffect` and every `referencesCombatOpponent()`; `BoostSelfWhenBlockingKeywordEffect`,
  `BoostSelfWhenCombatOpponentMatchesEffect` and its handler; `DestroyCombatOpponentAtEndOfCombatEffect.filter`;

  `regularBecomesBlocked`, `unfilteredTemporaryAndPersistentBecomesBlocked` and `hasEquipmentAttached`.
- New: `CombatBlockService.recordCombatOpponent`, `declaresChosenTarget` and `triggersOnceFor`; the block collector

  `fireBecomesBlockedTriggersWithoutBlockers` call `fireCreatureBecomesBlockedTriggers`.

**Cards (by script).** `scripts/step15-run17z11c-cards.py` (idempotent, per letter module): the 13
`DestroyCombatOpponentAtEndOfCombatEffect` cards' filters move to their triggers ("a creature" needs none: Venomous
Dragonfly, Tangle Asp, Infernal Medusa's blocks half); Corrosive Ooze's triggers filter `PermanentIsEquippedPredicate`;
the five `BoostSelfWhenBlockingKeywordEffect` cards are `Triggers.blocks().withFilter(new

#### Run 17z11c2: the "a creature (you control) becomes blocked" watchers record the blocked creature; the block pair is an event condition

Row 17z11c2, in one run, not split. The sites:

- `CombatBlockService.checkAllyBecomesBlockedTriggers` ("whenever a [filter] creature you control becomes blocked"):
  the entry's source was the blocked creature unless an effect was a `BoostReferencedPermanentEffect`, so the cards'
  "it" was written as self effects (`BoostSelfEffect`, `PutCountersOnSelfEffect`, `GrantKeywordEffect(SELF)`,
  `ReturnToHandEffect.self()`, Gustcloak Savior's untap and `RemoveSelfFromCombatEffect`, Ib Halfheart's
  `SacrificeSelfThenEffect`, `CreaturesBlockingSource()`, `PermanentBlockingSourcePredicate()`); a second pass with
  `eachBlocker` collected Retaliation's per-blocker ability.
- `checkAnyCreatureBecomesBlockedTriggers` ("whenever a creature becomes blocked", once per declared pair) read only
  `BlockPairConditionalEffect`s: it judged `firesForPair` on the pair's powers and the `attackerPredicate`, unwrapped
  `resolvedEffect()` and picked the attacker or the blocker by `actsOn()` as the non-targeting target (No Quarter's
  `DestroyWeakerBlockParticipantEffect`, Righteous Indignation's `BoostBlockerWhenAttackerMatchesEffect`).
- `checkBlockedCreatureTriggers` (the filtered once-per-attacker form, Spined Sliver and Berserk Murlodont) rebound the
  source to the blocked creature the same way, with no class read; it moved with the row.
- From run 17z11c's notes: a granted filtered "becomes blocked" ability without `EACH_BLOCKER` (Mirror Shield, Zombie
  Boa) was read as "becomes blocked by a creature" while a printed one is "by one or more".

**When the value is read.**

- Every "whenever a [filter] creature (you control) becomes blocked" entry has the watcher as its source (CR 113.7,
  checked) and records the blocked creature the same way whatever the effects are
  (`CombatBlockService.recordBlockedCreature`): its triggering permanent (id, controller, a last-known copy), its
  non-targeting target (CR 115.10a, checked) and its attacked target. "It" / "that creature" read the triggering
  permanent as the ability resolves; "for each creature blocking it" (`CreaturesBlockingSource(true)`) counts then
  (General Marhault's ruling). A target an effect takes is chosen as the ability goes on the stack, the choice carrying
  the blocked creature as its triggering permanent (Close Quarters).
- The filtered once-per-attacker watcher also judges the ability's event condition and intervening "if" on the blocked
  creature, for the watcher's controller, and skips a watcher that lost its abilities, as the other block readers do.
- "Whenever a creature becomes blocked by a creature" / "whenever a creature blocks a creature" (`EACH_BLOCKER` on
  `Triggers.creatureBecomesBlocked()`) is once for each declared attacker/blocker pair (CR 509.3b, 509.3d, checked):
  the attacker is the entry's triggering permanent and the blocker its non-targeting target, the trigger's filter is
  judged on the attacker and the ability's event condition on the pair as blockers are declared (CR 509.3f, checked).
  No Quarter's "with lesser power" is the new event condition `BlockPairLesserPower(BlockParticipant)`, so a later
  power change doesn't undo it, as before; "destroy the blocking creature" is `DestroyCombatOpponentEffect(false)`,
  "destroy the attacking creature" `DestroyReferencedPermanentEffect(TRIGGERING)` (neither checks that it is still a
  creature, as before). Righteous Indignation filters the attacker (black or red) and writes "the blocking creature
  gets +1/+1" as `BoostTargetCreatureEffect(1, 1)` with no declared target, "that creature".
- Ib Halfheart: "sacrifice it. If you do, it deals 4 damage to each creature blocking it" sacrifices the triggering
  permanent (`SacrificeSelfThenEffect.ofTriggeringPermanent`, nothing happens if it can't, as the ruling says) and the
  damage is dealt by it (`DealDamageToEachMatchingPermanentEffect.dealtByTriggeringPermanent()`, through
  `DamageSupport.entryDealtByTriggeringPermanent`, its last-known copy once sacrificed, CR 608.2h, checked), "blocking
  it" judged with it as the source. The copy is the one taken as the ability triggered, as the rebound source's
  snapshot was before.
- Labyrinth Raptor's "a creature … that's blocking it" is the new `PermanentBlockingSourcePredicate.ofTriggeringPermanent()`
  (the filter context's triggering permanent, else its last-known copy); `SacrificePermanentsEffectHandler`'s filter
  context now carries the entry's triggering permanent id.
- Retaliation ("creatures you control have 'whenever this creature becomes blocked by a creature, this creature gets
  +1/+1'") grants its ability (`GrantTriggeredAbilityEffect`, `GrantScope.ALL_OWN_CREATURES`), so the ally collector
  has no per-blocker pass: the creature is the ability's source and its controller controls it (CR 113.8, checked).
- A granted "becomes blocked" ability reads its options as a printed one does: `EACH_BLOCKER` once for each blocker
  (each granted ability an object of its own, CR 603.3, checked), with a filter on the blocker for each blocker it
  admits; without `EACH_BLOCKER` once if any blocker matches (CR 509.3c). Mirror Shield and Zombie Boa write
  `EACH_BLOCKER` ("becomes blocked by a creature with deathtouch / of that color"), so they trigger as before.

**May timing.** No "you may" moved: Cunning Evasion's, Grazilaxx's, Gustcloak Savior's and Norin's are asked as the
ability resolves (CR 603.5, checked), as before.

**Rules fixes.** None. Behaviour is unchanged for the converted cards in two-player games (all their cases pass
unchanged but Unstoppable Ash's source assertion, below).

Rulings (checked with `get_rulings`): Ib Halfheart (no sacrifice, no damage), Labyrinth Raptor (the defending player
sacrifices a blocker before combat damage; a planeswalker's controller is the defending player), General Marhault (the
count is as it resolves), Cunning Evasion (returned before combat damage), Seifer (deathtouch stays; triggers whoever
controls the attacker, below), Mirror Shield (the blocker's characteristics as it blocks), Grazilaxx (returned before
combat damage), Somberwald Alpha (once per blocked creature), Spined Sliver (two Slivers, +2/+2 for each blocker);
Gustcloak Savior, Retaliation, She-Hulk, Tattered Ratter, Unstoppable Ash, Berserk Murlodont, No Quarter, Righteous
Indignation and Zombie Boa have none.
The abilities agree with each.

**The model.**

- Gone: `BlockPairConditionalEffect`, `DestroyWeakerBlockParticipantEffect` and its handler,
  `BoostBlockerWhenAttackerMatchesEffect`; the ally collector's `eachBlocker` pass and `BoostReferencedPermanentEffect`
  read.
- New: the condition `BlockPairLesserPower(BlockParticipant)`; `PermanentBlockingSourcePredicate(PermanentReference)`
  (`SOURCE` by default, `ofTriggeringPermanent()`); `DealDamageToEachMatchingPermanentEffect.damageSource`
  (`dealtByTriggeringPermanent()`); `CombatBlockService.recordBlockedCreature`. `BlockParticipant` stays (the
  condition's).

**Cards (by script).** `scripts/step15-run17z11c2-cards.py` (idempotent, per letter module): Cunning Evasion, Grazilaxx,
General Marhault, Gustcloak Savior, Ib Halfheart, Labyrinth Raptor, Retaliation, Seifer, She-Hulk, Somberwald Alpha,
Tattered Ratter, Unstoppable Ash, Spined Sliver, Berserk Murlodont, No Quarter, Righteous Indignation, Mirror Shield and
Zombie Boa: 18 cards. Beastmaster's Magemark, Close Quarters and Norin already read the triggering permanent.

**Behaviour changes.**

- Every "a creature (you control) becomes blocked" entry has the watcher as its source and the blocked creature as its
  triggering permanent (with a last-known copy) and non-targeting target.
- The two any-creature readers skip a watcher that lost its abilities; the once-per-attacker one judges event
  conditions and accepts an unfiltered ability (none is written).
- Two Retaliations are two objects on the stack for each blocker (before, one entry with both boosts); the total is the
  same.
- Otherwise none intended.

**Left, and noted.**

- Seifer, Balamb Rival's "whenever a creature attacking one of your opponents becomes blocked by two or more
  creatures" triggers for any player's creature (its ruling); it is written on "a creature you control", which is the
  same in a two-player game. It could be `Triggers.creatureBecomesBlocked()` with the same event condition now that the
  once-per-attacker reader judges one; not done here (a multiplayer fix with no test).
- The pair reader runs only for declared blocks: a creature an effect makes block, or one put onto the battlefield
  blocking, doesn't trigger "becomes blocked by a creature" watchers (CR 509.3d says both do), and the once-per-attacker
  reader isn't called for an attacker an effect's blocker makes blocked or a token entering blocking makes blocked (CR
  509.3c). As before.
- `fireCreatureBecomesBlockedTriggers` still returns before reading continuously granted abilities when the attacker
  lost its printed abilities, whatever the timestamps (Retaliation entering after Humble grants the ability again,
  CR 613.7); as before.

#### Run 17z11d: the rest of `CombatAttackService` reads the event

Row 17z11d, in one run, not split. The sites (the audit's seven reads):

- The "whenever you attack" collector rebuilt a `GrantKeywordEffect(GrantScope.TARGETS)` with a filter, judging the
  filter on the attackers and dropping it (Frontier Warmonger), and gave the declared attackers as declared,
  non-targeting recipients to any `GrantKeywordEffect(TARGETS)` (Valor's Reach, Tyvar, Love on the Battlefield, Angelic
  Guardian); the planar collector did the same for Valor's Reach the plane (row 17z11f's read, done here with its
  card).
- `BoostCreaturesInAttackingBandsEffect` (Chatzuk): the collector fanned the ability out by band and gave the band as
  declared targets.
- Yotian Courier's `ChooseModeNotChosenDuringLastCombatEffect`: the self-attack collector filtered the options against
  the source's remembered mode and rebuilt a `ChooseOneEffect`.
- `grantedAbilityController`: a granted attack modal was controlled by the controller of the attached permanent whose
  static `GrantTriggeredAbilityEffect` equalled it (Pip-Boy 3000).
- `attackedTargetForPendingMay`: a "you may" wrapping `DealDamageToDefendingPlayerCreaturesEffect` had the defending
  player as its attacked target (Scalding Salamander, Ronin Cliffrider).

**When the value is read.**

- A "whenever you attack" entry records its attacking creatures whatever the effects are (as it already did), and
  "they / those creatures gain [keyword]" is the new `GrantScope.DECLARED_ATTACKERS`: the entry's attacking creatures,
  fixed as the ability triggered, wherever they are as it resolves (a creature removed from combat still gains it,
  as before). Frontier Warmonger's "attack one of your opponents or a planeswalker they control" is the trigger's
  filter (CR 603.2, checked), so the ability doesn't trigger without a matching attacker and "those creatures" are the
  matching ones, as before. The planar collector records the attacking player's attacking creatures the same way.
- "Whenever two or more creatures you control attack in a band" is the new `TriggerMultiplicity.EACH_BAND`: an ability
  of its own for each declared band of two or more (CR 702.22c, checked), whose attacking creatures (and count) are
  the band's; the effect reads them and boosts the ones still attacking in a band as it resolves, as before.
- Yotian Courier writes `ChooseOneAtTriggerTimeEffect(ChooseOneEffect.notChosenDuringLastCombat(...))`; the shared
  triggered-modal path leaves out the remembered mode and remembers the chosen one (CR 700.2b, checked), as By
  Elspeth's Command's does.
- A granted attack modal is the creature's ability, controlled by the creature's controller (CR 113.8, checked), as
  run 17z11b decided for the other granted abilities. Pip-Boy 3000's "whenever equipped creature attacks, choose one"
  is the Equipment's own printed ability (`Triggers.attacks()` on the Equipment): the attached reader queues its mode
  choice for the Equipment's controller with the Equipment as source and the attacking creature as the triggering
  permanent; "put a +1/+1 counter on that creature" is `PutCounterOnReferencedPermanentEffect(TRIGGERING, ...)`.
- Every self-attack "you may" entry has the attacked target and the defending player recorded whatever its effect is
  (CR 508.5, checked): `MayEffectHandler` already turns a gone attacked planeswalker or battle into the recorded
  defending player.

**May timing.** No "you may" moved: Scalding Salamander's and Ronin Cliffrider's are asked as the ability resolves (CR
603.5), as before.

**Rules fixes.**

- **An Equipment's "whenever equipped creature attacks" triggers for a creature that lost its abilities** (Pip-Boy
  3000): written as an ability granted to the creature, Humble (or any "loses all abilities") removed it. The new
  `PipBoy3000Test#equipmentsOwnAbilityTriggersForACreatureThatLostItsAbilities` fails at HEAD (below).

Rulings (checked with `get_rulings`): Pip-Boy 3000, Yotian Courier, Valor's Reach, Love on the Battlefield and Angelic
Guardian have none; Tyvar's are about its granted mana ability; Frontier Warmonger's is the multiplayer gap below;
Chatzuk is a playtest card with no data. The abilities agree with each.

**The model.**

- Gone: `ChooseModeNotChosenDuringLastCombatEffect`; `CombatAttackService.grantedAbilityController` and
  `attackedTargetForPendingMay`; the "you attack" collector's `GrantKeywordEffect` rebuild and declared recipients and
  its `BoostCreaturesInAttackingBandsEffect` read; the planar collector's `GrantKeywordEffect` read.
- New: `GrantScope.DECLARED_ATTACKERS` (the normal `GrantKeywordEffectHandler` grants to the entry's attacking

**Cards (by script).** `scripts/step15-run17z11d-cards.py` (idempotent, per letter module): Valor's Reach, Tyvar the

- The rules fix above.

- A self-attack "you may" entry records the defending player whatever its effect.

For step 16 (both runs): no new `Card`, `StackEntry`, `Permanent` or `GameData` state; an enum value each in

#### Run 17z11e: the step collectors record "that player" whatever the effects are; `EndStepPlayerTargetedEffect` is gone

Row 17z11e, split into 17z11e and 17z11e2: this run did the "that player" bindings of `StepTriggerService` (the end
step's, the draw step's, the opponent's and chosen player's upkeep's and the emblems'), the enchanted permanent's
controller of the your-end-step reader and the chosen-player `getOpponentId` fallback: 10 of the audit's 25 reads and
its last pick. The Aura grants, the payers, the rebuilds and the unwraps (14 reads) are row 17z11e2.

The sites:

- The each-end-step reader gave the end-step player as non-targeting `targetId` only to an
  `EndStepPlayerTargetedEffect` (a marker interface on eight records, `SequenceEffect`, `SacrificePermanentsEffect` and
  `PutCountersOnSelfEffect` among them) or a `ConditionalEffect` wrapping one, `null` otherwise; Impatience's
  `DealDamageIfDidntCastSpellThisTurnEffect` and Razor Pendulum's `DealDamageToEndStepPlayerIfLifeAtMostEffect` had
  branches of their own that judged their intervening "if" by class; the conditional "you may" branch gave the active
  player only to a `MayChoicePlayer.ACTIVE_PLAYER` choice (Ludevic, Necro-Alchemist; the row named Sygg, whose "you
  may" is its own).
- The emblem reader gave the active player as `targetId` only on an opponent's step.
- The each-draw-step reader skipped a tapped source by `DrawCardForTargetPlayerEffect.requireSourceUntapped` (Howling
  Mine) and made the entry non-targeting only for an untargeted `DrawCardForTargetPlayerEffect` or a
  `PutHandOnBottomOfLibraryAndDrawEffect`; every other each-draw-step entry had the active player as a *targeted*
  `targetId`.
- The opponent's-upkeep reader turned "each opponent's upkeep" into "the chosen player's upkeep" when the card had a
  `RememberTargetPlayerEffect` or `ChooseOpponentOnEnterEffect`, and with no chosen player picked
  `getOpponentId(original controller)`.
- The your-end-step reader gave a `DamageDealingEffect` of an attached source the attached permanent's controller as
  non-targeting `targetId` (Gremlin Infestation).

**When the value is read.**

- Every untargeted end-step, each-draw-step, opponent's and chosen player's upkeep and emblem entry records the player
  whose step it is the same way whatever its effects are (`StepTriggerService.recordStepPlayer`): as its active player,
  triggering player and non-targeting `targetId`, "that player", no target (CR 115.10a, checked). The effects read it
  as the ability resolves, as before. A target the card declares is chosen as the ability goes on the stack, as before.
- The end-step, each-draw-step and opponent's/chosen player's upkeep readers judge an intervening "if" with that player
  as the context target, as the opponent's-end-step reader already did: Impatience is
  `withInterveningIf(new EndStepPlayerDidntCastSpell(null))` and Razor Pendulum `withInterveningIf(new
  TargetPlayerLifeAtMost(5))`, each with `DealDamageToPlayersEffect(2, TRIGGERING_PLAYER)`; checked as the ability
  triggers and again as it resolves on the entry's `targetId` (CR 603.4, checked), as before.
  `EndStepPlayerDidntCastCreatureSpell` became `EndStepPlayerDidntCastSpell(CardType spellType)` (`null` any spell;
  Predatory Advantage `CREATURE`).
- Howling Mine's "if Howling Mine is untapped" is `withInterveningIf(new SourceUntapped())`, judged as it triggers and
  as it resolves on the source or its last-known information (its ruling); each-draw-step entries now record the
  source snapshot. `DrawCardForTargetPlayerEffect.requireSourceUntapped` is left with no card using it.
- "At the beginning of the chosen player's upkeep" is the new `ActivePlayer.CHOSEN_PLAYER`: the source's chosen player
  (its first chosen player id, else its remembered player), whoever controls the source (The Rack's and Black Vise's
  rulings); with none chosen the ability never triggers. A chosen player isn't a copiable value (CR 707.2, checked), so a
  permanent that becomes a copy of Black Vise has none. The Rack, Black Vise and Energy Vortex write it.
- An Aura's or Equipment's "at the beginning of your end step" entry records the permanent it is attached to
  (`attachedPermanentSnapshot`) whatever its effects; the departure refresh records that permanent's controller as it
  leaves, and `DealDamageToEnchantedPermanentControllerEffectHandler` reads "enchanted artifact's controller" from the
  live attachment, else that last-known controller (CR 608.2h, checked), else the dies trigger's `targetId` (row 17z11f's
  bake).

**May timing.** No "you may" moved: Sygg's, Ludevic's and the each-end-step "you may"s are asked as the ability
resolves (CR 603.5, checked), as before. Intervening "if"s: unchanged timing (trigger and resolution).

**Rules fixes.**

- **"That player" of an each-draw-step ability isn't a target** (Malignant Growth, Mornsong Aria, Maralen of the
  Mornsong, Anvil of Bogardan, Omen Machine, Academy Loremaster): the entry had the active player as
  a targeted `targetId`, so a player with shroud or hexproof made the ability do nothing. The new
  `MalignantGrowthTest#thatPlayerWithShroudStillDrawsAndTakesDamage` gives the opponent Ivory Mask; it fails at HEAD
  (below).
- **"The chosen player's upkeep" needs a chosen player** (Black Vise, The Rack, Energy Vortex): with none, the collector
  picked the original controller's opponent (`getOpponentId`, one of them in multiplayer). The new
  `BlackViseTest#copyWithoutChosenPlayerDoesNotTrigger` makes Mizzium Transreliquat a copy of Black Vise; only the
  original triggers. It fails at HEAD (below).

Rulings (checked with `get_rulings`): Impatience (a countered spell counts), Razor Pendulum (none), Howling Mine (no
trigger when tapped, checked again as it resolves, last-known tap state), Ludevic (checked only as it resolves: its

#### Run 17z11e2: the Aura grants are granted abilities, the payers and the Flux family read the event; Giant Oyster is split off

Row 17z11e2, split into 17z11e2 and 17z11e3: this run did 12 of the audit's 14 reads. Giant Oyster's two (a printed
draw-step ability the reader skips by class, and a class-keyed reader that finds the locked permanents and the lock's
activator) are row 17z11e3: its counters are a delayed triggered ability of the activation (CR 603.7, checked), a model
change of its own.

The sites:

- The enchanted-controller upkeep reader made an Aura's ability the creature's by class
  (`SacrificeEnchantedCreatureEffect.grantedToCreature` and Shifting Shadow's effect's flag swapped the source,
  controller and triggering permanent), skipped Withercrown's `ForcedCostOrElseEffect` by its cost's class and predicate
  when a later "loses all abilities" removed the grant, and built Custody Battle's "target opponent" filter for a
  `ForcedCostOrElseEffect` whose else effects held a `TargetPlayerGainsControlOfEnchantedPermanentEffect`.
- The enchanted-controller end-step reader made Nettlevine Blight's `SacrificeEnchantedPermanentAndReattachSourceAuraEffect`
  the enchanted permanent's (controller, source id) and skipped it by class when the grant was removed.
- The each-upkeep reader exempted a `ForcedCostOrElseEffect` with `payerIsEnchantedController` from every target branch
  (Pillar Tombs of Aku's "that player", Fraying Line's paid rope counter).
- The your-upkeep reader kept Call to the Kindred's "you may" out of the may branch by its wrapped effect's class, so
  that the plain entry recorded the enchanted creature.
- `handleGrantedArtifactSacrificeTriggers` rebuilt a `ForcedCostOrElseEffect` for every permanent an
  `AllPermanentsUpkeepSacrificeUnlessPayEffect` covered (Energy Flux and six more), with its own removed-grant check.
- The your-end-step reader judged Admiral Beckett Brass's `GainControlIfSubtypesDealtCombatDamageEffect` by class and
  rebuilt a `GainControlOfTargetEffect` with the qualifying controllers baked in.
- The saga and beginning-of-combat readers choose a `ChooseOneAtRandomEffect`'s mode as the ability triggers.

What the probe found (a temporary log in the each-upkeep branch, removed, over the test classes of every card with an
each-upkeep ability, 146 classes, all passing at HEAD): the player-only target effects were the Oaths' "you may"s
(declared by the card) and Pillar Tombs of Aku's payment (not declared); Magmatic Force's "any target" is declared by
its effect, not the card. So "that player" is exactly a player-only target the card doesn't declare, the rule run
17z11b gave the damage collectors; an any-target or permanent target is chosen as before.

**When the value is read.**

- "Enchanted creature / permanent has '…'" is a `GrantTriggeredAbilityEffect`: Necrotic Plague's `SacrificeSelfEffect`,
  Shifting Shadow's `DestroySelfThenRevealUntilCreatureAndAttachGrantingAuraEffect`, Withercrown's
  `ForcedCostOrElseEffect(SacrificePermanentCost(PermanentIsSourcePermanentPredicate), [LoseLifeEffect(1, CONTROLLER)],
  true)` (as Town-Razer Tyrant's grant), Custody Battle's `ForcedCostOrElseEffect(sacrifice a land,
  [TargetPlayerGainsControlOfSourceCreatureEffect()], true)`, Nettlevine Blight's end-step ability. The permanent is the
  ability's source and its controller controls it (CR 113.7, 113.8, checked; the Necrotic Plague and Nettlevine Blight
  rulings say so); a later "loses all abilities" removes it in layer 6 (CR 613.1f, checked) as the layer system computes
  the grant, so no reader checks the removal.
- The your-upkeep and your-end-step readers record a granted ability's granting Aura on its entry
  (`StackEntry.requireGrantingPermanentId()`, through the new `StepAbilityReader.effects(..., abilityByEffect)` identity
  map, as `CombatAbilityReader.grantingPermanents` does). "Attach Shifting Shadow / Nettlevine Blight" reads it as the
  ability resolves: an Aura that has left isn't attached, a creature that has left isn't destroyed, and the cards are
  revealed either way (Shifting Shadow's rulings); "you" reveals and sacrifices as the ability's controller.
- A granted your-upkeep ability's player target is chosen with the ability's own target filter
  (`TriggeredAbility.targetFilter()`, which the your-upkeep reader now reads too): Custody Battle's "target opponent", an
  opponent of the creature's controller, chosen as the ability goes on the stack (CR 603.3d, checked).
- An each-upkeep player-only target the card doesn't declare is "that player", the entry's non-targeting active player
  (CR 115.10a, checked). `ForcedCostOrElseEffect.targetSpec()` leaves out a "that player" payment's paid effects
  (Fraying Line's rope counter is put by the payer once they have paid, no target), so no reader exempts the class.
- An Aura's or Equipment's your-upkeep "you may" entry records the permanent it is attached to, whatever its effect
  (Call to the Kindred's "shares a creature type with enchanted creature", its last-known information once it has left,
  CR 608.2h, checked); `GameData.queueMayAbility(..., activePlayerId, snapshot)` returns its entry.
- "All artifacts / creatures have '…'" (Energy Flux, Kataki, Pendrell Mists, Magus of the Tabernacle, Vile Consumption,
  The Tabernacle at Pendrell Vale) and "other enchantments have '…'" (Aura Flux) are `GrantTriggeredAbilityEffect`s of a
  `Triggers.upkeep(YOU)` `ForcedCostOrElseEffect` (`PayManaCost` or `PayLifeCost(1)`; `SacrificeSelfEffect` or
  `DestroyReferencedPermanentEffect(SOURCE)`): "all creatures" is `ALL_CREATURES_INCLUDING_SELF`, "all artifacts"
  `ALL_PERMANENTS` and `SELF` with the artifact filter (the source too while it is an artifact, as the marker had it),
  "other enchantments" `ALL_PERMANENTS`. The ability is each permanent's own, on its controller's upkeep.
- Admiral Beckett Brass's "target nonland permanent controlled by a player who was dealt combat damage by three or more
  Pirates this turn" is the card's target filter with the new
  `PermanentControllerDealtCombatDamageBySubtypeThisTurnPredicate(PIRATE, 3)`, judged as the target is chosen and again
  as the ability resolves. It is a target restriction, not an intervening "if" (the Oracle text has no "if"): the ability
  triggers and, with no legal target, is removed (CR 603.3d), which looks the same as the old skip.
- "Choose one at random" picks its mode as the ability goes on the stack, before its targets, which only an eligible
  mode can have (CR 603.3c, 700.2b, checked), as the readers do for a "choose one": the class picks the path, no event is
  read. The audit classifies these two reads ROUTE, with `ChooseOneEffect`'s.

**May timing.** No "you may" moved: Call to the Kindred's, the granted payments' (Withercrown's, Custody Battle's, the

#### Run 17z11e3: Giant Oyster's draw-step counters and counter removal are delayed triggered abilities its activation creates

Row 17z11e3, done: the audit's two reads. Giant Oyster had a printed `Triggers.drawStep(YOU)` ability with
`PutCountersOnUntapLockedPermanentsEffect`, which the your-draw-step reader skipped by class, and a second class-keyed
reader that found the Oyster by that effect, its locked permanents and the lock's activator
(`GameData.untapLockActivatorBySource`); the counter removal was a static marker (`RemoveCountersWhenUntapLockEndsEffect`)
that `UntapLockReleaseService` read off the card, with the same activator map.

**When the value is read.**

- The Oyster's ruling says the activation creates three things: a continuous effect for as long as it stays tapped (the
  untap lock, unchanged), "a repeating delayed triggered ability that's in effect only as long as Giant Oyster remains
  tapped", and "a delayed triggered ability that triggers when Giant Oyster untaps or when it leaves the battlefield".
  The activation's effects now say so: `RegisterDelayedDrawStepTriggerWhileSourceTappedEffect(new
  PutCounterOnTargetPermanentEffect(MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE, 1))` and `RegisterDelayedSourceUntapsOrLeavesTriggerEffect(new
  RemoveAllCountersEffect(MINUS_ONE_MINUS_ONE, TARGET))`, after the lock.
- Both delayed abilities are the activator's (CR 603.7e, checked: an activated ability's delayed trigger is controlled by
  the player who controlled that ability; the old comments cited 603.7d, which is about spells), so "each of your draw
  steps" stays the activator's after the Oyster changes control, and neither depends on the Oyster's abilities.
- The draw-step ability (`DelayedDrawStepTriggerWhileSourceTapped`) is created only while the Oyster is still tapped from
  that activation (its untap count unchanged), as the lock is; `StepTriggerService` puts it on the stack at the beginning
  of each of its controller's draw steps, aimed at "that creature" without targeting it, and ends it when the Oyster has
  untapped or left or the creature has left (CR 603.7c: a new object isn't "that creature"). Its counter is put on as
  it resolves even if the Oyster untapped in response (the 2004 ruling), as before.
- The removal (`DelayedSourceUntapsOrLeavesTrigger`) is created whenever the ability resolves with the Oyster on the
  battlefield, tapped or not: an Oyster that untapped before its ability resolved triggers it the next time it untaps
  (CR 603.7a's second example, checked). `UntapLockReleaseService`, called from the untap paths and the battlefield
  removal, releases the locks, ends the draw-step abilities and puts the removal on the stack.

**May timing.** No "you may" involved. Intervening "if"s: none.

**Rules fix.**

- **An Oyster untapped before its ability resolves still removes the counters when it next untaps** (CR 603.7a): at HEAD
  no removal was created without a lock. The new `GiantOysterTest#oysterUntappedBeforeResolutionStillRemovesCountersWhenItNextUntaps`
  untaps the Oyster in response, taps it again and untaps it in its controller's untap step: the creature's -1/-1
  counter is removed. It fails at HEAD (below).

Rulings (checked with `get_rulings`): the four Giant Oyster rulings (a tapped creature only; the activation's three
parts; activated during upkeep, a counter in the following draw step; the counter trigger resolves after an untap's
removal). The abilities agree with each.

**The model.**

- Gone: `PutCountersOnUntapLockedPermanentsEffect` (and its handler), `RemoveCountersWhenUntapLockEndsEffect`,
  `GameData.untapLockActivatorBySource`, Giant Oyster's printed draw-step ability and static marker, the draw-step
  reader's skip and the Oyster reader.
- New: `RegisterDelayedDrawStepTriggerWhileSourceTappedEffect`, `RegisterDelayedSourceUntapsOrLeavesTriggerEffect` (and
  their handlers), the `DelayedAction`s `DelayedDrawStepTriggerWhileSourceTapped` and `DelayedSourceUntapsOrLeavesTrigger`,
  `StepTriggerService.collectDelayedDrawStepTriggersWhileSourceTapped`; `UntapLockReleaseService` drains and ends the
  delayed actions instead of reading a static marker.

**Cards (by script).** `scripts/step15-run17z11e3-cards.py`: Giant Oyster.

**Behaviour changes.** The rules fix; the draw-step and removal abilities are named "Giant Oyster's delayed ability";
otherwise none intended.

For step 16: no new `Card`, `StackEntry` or `Permanent` state; `GameData` loses a map, and its delayed-action queue gains
two immutable kinds (copied with it); nothing new is slot-keyed.

**Scripts.** `scripts/step15-run17z11e3-cards.py`, `scripts/step15-run17z11e3-tests.py` (idempotent; optional
repository-root argument, used for the HEAD worktree) and `scripts/step15-run17z11e3-docs.py` (idempotent; fails if a
doc or skill still names a removed form outside a "Gone" line: `ORACLE_TEXT_EFFECT_MAP.md`,
`CARD_PATTERNS_ABILITIES_WALKERS_SAGAS.md`, `EFFECTS_QUICK_REFERENCE.md`, `EFFECTS_INDEX.md`). `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s
becomes-the-target paragraph (run 17z11f) also names the delayed abilities.

**Tests changed.** Card (by script): the new case above. Giant Oyster's other 16 cases are unchanged and pass.

**Test runs.**

- Card: Giant Oyster's class and those of the other untap-lock cards (Rust Tick, Ice Floe, Amber Prison), 68 cases, all
  passing; then again in run 17z11f's card run (below), with Whip Vine, Thalakos Dreamsower, Sand Squid, Phyrexian

#### Run 17z11f: the becomes-the-target collectors record the spell or ability that targeted whatever the effects are

Row 17z11f, split into 17z11f, 17z11f2 and 17z11f3: this run did the row's first item, the becomes-the-target
collectors' counter and triggering-spell reads, and Chancellor of the Annex's opening-hand counter (the cast collector's
read of the same kind): 16 of the audit's 52 reads, and the two ROUTE reads of the ward log lines. The "when you cast
this spell" collector (cascade, demonstrate, ripple, its triggering-spell marker, a granted cascade's single copy) and
Venser's emblem are row 17z11f2: the self-cast "you may" is asked before the ability goes on the stack there, and moving
it to resolution (CR 603.5) touches about 23 cards and their tests, a run of its own. The rest of the row's reads are
row 17z11f3.

The sites:

- Six becomes-the-target collectors put a `CounterUnlessEffect` (ward and the other "counter it unless" abilities) or a
  `CounterSpellingEffect` on an entry of its own aimed at the targeting spell or ability in the stack zone, by class;
  the "you become the target" collector dropped every other effect.
- Three collectors split `TriggeringSpellReferencingEffect`s (Forsaken Wastes, Bonecrusher Giant, Retromancer, Lava
  Runner, Fractured Loyalty, Thunderbreak Regent) onto an entry pointed at the targeting object's card, with that
  object's controller baked into `triggeringPermanentControllerId`, and made the entry non-targeting only for a
  `DealDamageToTriggeringSpellControllerEffect`.
- `collectBecomesTargetOfSpellOrAbilityTriggers` judged "for the first time each turn" for any `CounterSpellEffect`
  (Glyph Keeper, the Glasskites, Kira's grant), whatever the card said.
- The ward suppression and removal checks and the attached-permanent dispatch identified ward by
  `isCounterUnlessTrigger` (a `CounterUnlessEffect`, or one inside an intervening "if").
- The cast collector put Chancellor of the Annex's opening-hand trigger on the stack only for a `CounterUnlessEffect`.

What the probe found (a temporary log in `TargetAbilityReader.read`, removed, over the test classes of every card with
a becomes-the-target trigger, a counter-unless, counterspelling or triggering-spell effect, ward or Strict Proctor's
marker: 755 classes, 6,402 cases, all passing at HEAD): every effect that acts on a spell in a becomes-the-target
ability is a counter-unless effect, `CounterSpellEffect` (Glyph Keeper's family) or one of two that also admit a
creature (Monk Gyatso's "airbend that creature or spell", whose entry already refers to the creature, and backup's copy,
whose entry refers to the backup ability); "you become the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls" has
only `CounterUnlessPaysEffect` (Amulet of Safekeeping, Valkmira); no card declares a spell target in such an ability; and no "for the first time each turn"
ability has a limit other than Glyph Keeper's family's implicit one.

**When the value is read.**

- Every becomes-the-target entry records the spell or ability that targeted as its triggering spell (a copy as it was
  then; `CopySupport.triggeringSpell` reads it live while it is on the stack and as it last existed there once it has
  left, CR 608.2h) and its controller as its triggering player, whatever its effects are
  (`TriggerCollectionService.enqueueTargetTriggeredAbility` / `recordTargetingObject`, in every becomes-the-target
  collector that puts the ability on the stack itself, the activated-ability and backup watchers included).
- "That spell or ability" is not targeted (CR 702.21a's ward and the other cards say "counter it", "counter that spell
  or ability"): an entry with no other referent whose effect acts only on a spell is aimed at that object on the stack,
  non-targeting, the rule run 17z11b gave "that player". Which abilities go on the stack apart from the others is now
  that rule too, not a class (ward stays its own object, CR 603.3).
- "That spell's / that spell or ability's controller" (Forsaken Wastes, Bonecrusher Giant, Retromancer, Thunderbreak
  Regent, Lava Runner, Fractured Loyalty) is the controller of the triggering spell, read as the ability resolves: it
  still loses life, takes the damage or sacrifices after the object was countered or resolved (Bonecrusher Giant's
  ruling), and a control change of the spell meanwhile is seen.
- "For the first time each turn" is the trigger's `TriggerLimit.FIRST_TIME_EACH_TURN` on Glyph Keeper, Shimmering
  Glasskite, Jetting Glasskite and Kira, Great Glass-Spinner's grant; the becomes-the-target-of-a-spell-or-ability
  collector judges it with the permanent's "targeted this turn" mark as before (every targeting counts, also one before
  the ability was granted), and `TriggeredAbility` accepts the limit on that trigger.
- Ward is identified as an ability that acts only on a spell (for ward suppression, a removed ward keyword and an
  attached permanent's granted ward), not by a counter class.
- Chancellor of the Annex's opening-hand trigger records the first spell as its triggering spell and player and acts on
  it without targeting it.

**May timing.** No "you may" moved: "you become the target of a spell" abilities with a "you may" were already put on
the stack and asked as they resolve (CR 603.5); they now go through the same entry. Intervening "if"s: an intervening
"if" around a ward counter is judged as before.

**Rules fixes.** None found: the recorded values are the ones the class branches bound. The entries are non-targeting
where a counter entry of Glyph Keeper's family targeted the triggering object before (it doesn't target).

Rulings (checked with `get_rulings`): Bonecrusher Giant (resolves even if the spell is countered; once per spell),
Glyph Keeper (embalm only), Kira and Jetting Glasskite (none). The abilities agree with each.

**The model.**

- Gone from `TriggerCollectionService`: the counter-unless, counterspelling, `CounterSpellEffect`, triggering-spell and
  `DealDamageToTriggeringSpellControllerEffect` reads, `isCounterUnlessTrigger`, the ransom-kind log switch.
- New: `recordTargetingObject`, `actsOnASpell`; `enqueueTargetTriggeredAbility(gameData, targetingEntry, entry)`; the

- `DealDamageToTriggeringSpellControllerEffectHandler`, `TriggeringObjectControllerGainsControlOfEnchantedPermanentEffectHandler`,
  `TriggeringSpellControllerSacrificesPermanentsEffectHandler` and `TargetSpellControllerLosesLifeEffectHandler` (a

- `TriggeredAbility.requireFirstTimeReader` accepts `Triggers.becomesTargetOfSpellOrAbility()`;
  `TriggeringSpellReferencingEffect`'s Javadoc says only the self-cast collector still reads it.

**Cards (by script).** `scripts/step15-run17z11f-cards.py`: Glyph Keeper, Shimmering Glasskite, Jetting Glasskite,
Kira, Great Glass-Spinner.

**Behaviour changes.** Becomes-the-target entries record the triggering spell and player; the counter entries of Glyph

#### Run 17z11f2: the "when you cast this spell" collector puts each ability on the stack and records the spell whatever the effects are

Row 17z11f2, done: the audit's five reads and two of the same kind outside its files.

The sites:

- `TriggerCollectionService.collectSelfCastEffects` took the effects of all the card's "when you cast this spell"
  abilities as one list and sorted them by class: a "copy this spell" effect (`copiesThisSpell`), a `CascadeEffect` and
  a demonstrate `MayEffect` (`DemonstrateEffect.isWrappedBy`) each got an entry of its own, built three ways (the copy's
  with the triggering spell, cascade's with the X and kick only, demonstrate's with the triggering spell and a log line);
  a lone untargeted `MayEffect` but ripple's was asked before the ability was on the stack
  (`PendingMayAbility.forSpellCastTrigger`); everything else went on the stack as one object, given the spell as its
  triggering card only when an effect was a `TriggeringSpellReferencingEffect`.
- `collectSpellAbility` made a cast ability whose effects were all `CascadeEffect`s a "single copy" (no additional
  triggers), and `SpellCastTriggerCollectorService.handleGenericSpellCastTrigger` split several `CascadeEffect`s into
  entries sourced by the spell, both by class.
- Venser, the Sojourner's emblem held `ExileTargetOnControllerSpellCastEffect`, a marker the cast collector read by
  class to queue an `ExileTargetPermanentEffect` target choice.

What the probe found (a temporary log at each branch, removed, over the test classes of every card with a "when you
cast this spell" ability, cascade, demonstrate, ripple or replicate (printed or granted), a cast-trigger grant or a
perpetual grant, and Venser: 327 classes, all passing at HEAD):

- The pre-stack "you may" path was taken by two cards only, Conduit of Ruin and The Master, Formed Anew (the row's
  "about 23" counted every self-cast card with a "you may"; the others are targeted, a `MayPayManaEffect`, ripple or
  demonstrate, which already went on the stack).
- Every cascade, demonstrate and copy effect that took its own branch was an ability of its own on its card.
- Eleven cards wrote one Oracle ability as several `addTrigger`s, which the merge put back together: Abundant Maw,
  Decimator of the Provinces, Flayer of Loyalties, Gluttonous Hellkite, Hydroid Krasis, Hideous Taskmaster, Kozilek,
  Compleated, Mutated Cultist, Oblivion Sower, Sauron, Lord of the Rings, The Beast, Deathless Prince (each checked
  against its Oracle text: one ability); and Wingbright Thief's perpetual grant was built as one ability per effect.
- The "single copy" read was hit by Imoti, Zhulodok, TARDIS Bay and Wild-Magic Sorcerer, whose cascade is granted to the
  spell, and by Jodah, the Unifier, whose ability is its own.

**When the value is read.**

- Each "when you cast this spell" ability (the card's own, a granted replicate or demonstrate, a perpetually granted
  one) is one object on the stack (CR 603.3), a keyword's as any other; several instances of cascade trigger separately
  (CR 702.85c). `collectSelfCastAbilities` puts an untargeted ability on the stack with the spell recorded as its
  triggering spell (`recordTriggeringSpell`: the spell, its places in the turn's cast order, X, repeatable cost
  payments and casualty) and its kick and cast zone, whatever the effects are; a targeted one chooses its targets as it
  goes on the stack (CR 603.3d), as before.
- Cascade's "this spell's mana value" (CR 702.85a) is read as the ability resolves from the triggering spell
  (`TargetSpellManaValue`: the spell on the stack with its X, or as it last existed there once it has left, CR 608.2h),
  for a spell's own cascade too (it read the card's mana value and the entry's X before; the same number). Imoti's
  ruling: a countered spell's cascade still resolves.
- "Spells you cast … have cascade" is `Triggers.youCastSpell().withFilter(…).grantedToTheSpell()` (the new
  `SpellFilter.grantedToTheSpell`): the ability is the spell's (CR 113.1a, 113.7), each effect an ability of its own
  sourced by the spell, and nothing that makes the permanent's abilities trigger additional times applies; Imoti,
  Zhulodok ("cascade, cascade"), TARDIS Bay and Wild-Magic Sorcerer by script. Jodah, the Unifier's "whenever you cast a
  legendary nontoken spell from your hand, exile cards …" is Jodah's own ability (its rulings), so it is written without.
- Venser's emblem is `CreateEmblemEffect(new TriggeredAbility(Triggers.youCastSpell(), new ExileTargetPermanentEffect()),
  …)`, read by the emblem cast reader, its target chosen as it goes on the stack; each emblem triggers separately (its
  ruling).

**May timing.** Conduit of Ruin's and The Master, Formed Anew's "you may" are asked as the ability resolves (CR 603.5,
checked): the ability goes on the stack above the spell, and players may respond before the choice. Their tests passed
priority before answering already and are unchanged. Intervening "if"s: unchanged (judged as the ability triggers and
again as it resolves).

**Rules fixes.**

- **Jodah, the Unifier's ability is its own** (Roaming Throne naming Human makes it trigger an additional time): the
  class-keyed single copy treated it as a granted cascade. The new
  `JodahTheUnifierTest#roamingThroneDoublesJodahsAbility` fails at HEAD (one Jodah trigger, below).
- **A self-cast "you may" goes on the stack before it is asked** (Conduit of Ruin, The Master, Formed Anew; CR 603.5):
  the new `ConduitOfRuinTest#castTriggerAsksItsMayAsItResolves` (the trigger on the stack above the spell and no
  question until it resolves) fails at HEAD.

Rulings (checked with `get_rulings`): Jodah, the Unifier (the ability and the spell it casts resolve before the
triggering spell; mana value with X), Imoti (cascade resolves before the spell, also if it is countered; Imoti leaving
after the cast doesn't stop it), Venser (the emblem is the ability's source; each emblem triggers separately), Conduit
of Ruin and The Master, Formed Anew (nothing on the cast ability). The abilities agree with each.

**The model.**

- Gone: `TriggeringSpellReferencingEffect` (its 22 implementers implement `CardEffect` or their other capability
  interface), `ExileTargetOnControllerSpellCastEffect`, `PendingMayAbility.forSpellCastTrigger`,
  `DemonstrateEffect.isWrappedBy`, `collectSelfCastEffects` and `copiesThisSpell`, the singleCopy and multi-cascade
  class reads, Venser's emblem branch.
- New: `SpellFilter.grantedToTheSpell` (a component) with `SpellFilter.withGrantedToTheSpell()` and
  `SpellTrigger.grantedToTheSpell()`; `TriggerCollectionService.collectSelfCastAbilities` and

The sites:

  `PutCardToBattlefieldEffect` with a mana value bound, and as its triggering power only for a `ConditionalEffect` on

  (`RegisterDelayedReturnDyingCreatureUnderControlEffect` in `staticEffects`) on the stack by its class.

  ability triggered, dropping the branch of the other outcome.

  trigger-time mode choice, and the ally-tap reader routed one there by its class.
- `triggerAnotherPermanentLeaves` and the scheme leave reader skipped a `TransformSelfWhenChosenPermanentLeavesEffect`
  unless the leaving permanent was the source's chosen one, and recorded the source's snapshot only for it.

  `GainLifeEffect(damage)` entry; `checkEmblemAllyCreatureCombatDamageToPlayerTriggers` rebuilt Kaito Shizuki's emblem
