#### Run 17z13e2: the tap-for-mana, untap-step and library watches have one default each (rows 17z13e2 and 17z13e6)

Rows 17z13e2 and 17z13e6, done. Step 15 stays open (rows 17z13e3 to 17z13e5, 17z13e7 and 17z13e8).

**What the reading found** (each handler of `step15-run17z13e-audit.py --watch TapWatch` and `--watch LibraryWatch` read,
its cards found by a grep of their triggers and effect classes and read against their Oracle text):

- "Whenever a player taps a land for mana" had a default, but 17 class-keyed handlers judged the ability's trigger
  condition from the effect's class or fields: "enchanted land" (the Auras' `AddManaOnEnchantedLandTapEffect`, C.A.M.P.,
  by `getAttachedTo()`), "you tap" (five effects' `controllerOnly`, Savage Firecat's, Sasaya's Essence's and Forsaken
  Monument's handler checks), "an opponent taps" (War's Toll, Mana Web), "this land" (Forbidden Orchard, Rainbow Vale,
  `sourceOnly`), the land's subtype (`AddManaWhenLandOfSubtypeTappedForManaEffect`, Snowfall), its name (Extraplanar
  Lens's `matchesImprintedCardName`), "while you're the monarch" (Regal Behemoth's `monarchOnly`) and Price of Glory's
  intervening "if" ("if it's not that player's turn", judged as the land was tapped and never as the ability resolved,
  CR 603.4). The triggered mana abilities (CR 605.1b) added their mana inside the handlers: only
  `AddOneOfEachManaTypeProducedByLandEffect`, `AddManaForEachOtherLandWithSameNameEffect` and the sequences went through an
  entry and the effects' handlers; Runaway Growth's sequence had a branch of its own. Each recorded what it needed: the
  land for some, the player for others, nothing for the mana ones.
- Every one of them is the card's ability; the engine makes only Selesnya Loft Gardens' "until end of turn, whenever
  you tap a land for mana" (a floating effect `checkLandTapTriggers` reads), whose "you" was the granted effect's
  `controllerOnly`. Rainbow Vale's "An opponent gains control of this land at the beginning of the next end step" is part
  of its mana ability (Oracle text; rulings: "If Rainbow Vale's ability is activated …"), written as a land-tap trigger,
  so it fired for any mana ability of the land.
- "Whenever a player taps a permanent for mana" and the three "whenever you tap a creature / a nonland permanent / an
  artifact token for mana" watches (`ManaTapTriggerCollectorService`) had no default: Treasure Nabber's handler judged
  "an opponent" and "an artifact", the mana handlers added mana directly; an effect no handler named didn't trigger.
  "Whenever you untap one or more permanents during your untap step" had one handler (The Millennium Calendar's), which
  recorded the count only when the amount named it.
- Piracy ("you may tap lands you don't control for mana") makes the player who taps a land and its controller two
  players: "its controller adds" (Wild Growth and the other Auras, Vernal Bloom, Gauntlet of Might and of Power, Snowfall)
  is the land's controller, "add" (Crypt Ghast, Caged Sun, Groundchuck & Dirtbag) the ability's controller, "that player
  adds" (Mana Flare) the tapper. The first card-test run of the new default, which gave every "adds" to the tapper,
  failed `OvergrowthTest`, `VernalBloomTest` and `SnowfallTest`'s Piracy cases.
- The library watches: "whenever a player cycles a card" had no default (six handlers; the `Cycle` context fell through
  `recordDiscard`, so none recorded the cycle). The discard defaults returned `false` for a targeted effect, so each
  targeted ability needed a handler of its own class (Ominous Sphinx, Zenith Seeker, the counter and fight handlers),
  and their `DiscardControllerTriggerTarget` carried no discard. The scry default recorded no scrying player and judged
  The Temporal Anchor's "whenever you choose to put one or more cards on the bottom of your library while scrying" by its
  effect's class (`ExileBottomCardsToSourceEffect` with an `EventValue` count and nothing bottomed: no trigger). The
  surveil default recorded neither the surveilling player nor the source, and its `PutCountersOnSelfEffect` handler
  dropped the "do this only once each turn" mark.

**What changed.**

- `LandTapTriggerCollectorService` is the tap-for-mana default, for "a player taps a land for mana" and for the four
  permanent watches (`ManaTapTriggerCollectorService` is gone): the entry records the tapping player as its triggering
  player, the tapped permanent as its triggering permanent with its last-known snapshot (CR 608.2h: Gemstone Mine's last
  use), its non-targeting "that player" (a land's tap) or "that permanent" (a permanent's), the produced mana colors, the
  source's snapshot or face-up plane and the "do this only once each turn" mark, whatever the effects are. A triggered
  mana ability (`TapAbilityReader.isTriggeredManaEffect`: no target, could add mana) resolves at once through its effects'
  handlers (CR 605.4a), waiting in `pendingManaAbilityTriggers` while the permanent's own any-color choice is open when an
  effect `readsProducedMana()` (new on `TriggeredManaAbilityEffect`); a targeted ability (Forbidden Orchard, C.A.M.P.)
  goes to `SpellTargetTriggerAnyTarget` carrying the same record (CR 603.3d), after that choice when the produced mana
  isn't known; any other goes on the stack. The 17 land-tap and 5 mana-tap handlers are gone.
- The relation the handlers judged is the trigger's: `TapTrigger.judgedTapRelation()` (was `opponentTapsLand()`) reads
  "you tap a land", "an opponent taps a land / a permanent", "enchanted land is tapped" and "you tap this land" by the
  "a player taps a land / a permanent for mana" watch keys, `TapAbilityReader.TapEffect.tapRelation()` (was
  `opponentTaps()`) carries it, and `TriggerCollectionService.tapForManaMatches` (was `landTapMatches`) judges it for the
  land watch and, with the filter, for "a player taps a permanent for mana". New triggers `Triggers.youTapLandForMana()`,
  `enchantedLandTappedForMana()`, `youTapThisLandForMana()`, `opponentTapsPermanentForMana()`. The land-tap judge gives
  an intervening "if" the tapping player as "that player" (`withTargetId`), as the entry gives it as it resolves. The
  floating Selesnya Loft Gardens loop judges "you" against the affected player.
- The mana effects lost their trigger-condition fields and gained handlers (they added mana in the collector):
  `AddManaOnEnchantedLandTapEffectHandler`, `AddExtraManaOfChosenColorOnLandTapEffectHandler`,
  `AddManaWhenTappedForManaEffectHandler`, `AddManaWhenLandOfColorTappedForManaEffectHandler`,
  `AddRestrictedManaWhenLandTappedForManaEffectHandler`; `AddManaOfTypeProducedByTappedPermanentEffectHandler` reads a
  required color among several produced and offers a choice among several types. `AddManaWhenLandOfSubtypeTappedForManaEffect`
  and `AddManaWhenCreatureTappedForManaEffect` are gone into `AddManaWhenTappedForManaEffect` (renamed from
  `AddManaWhenLandTappedForManaEffect`; `ofItsController` for "its controller adds"), Snowfall's effect is
  `AddRestrictedManaWhenLandTappedForManaEffect` (renamed, its subtype the filter), `AddOneOfEachManaTypeProducedByLandEffect`
  keeps only `anyColor` (`ofAnyColor()`), `AddExtraManaOfChosenColorOnLandTapEffect` only "its controller adds"
  (`ofItsController()`). "Its controller adds" is `TappedLandManaSupport.tappedPermanentController` (the permanent's
  controller on the battlefield, else the tapper). New predicate `PermanentSharesNameWithImprintedCardPredicate`
  (Extraplanar Lens's filter). Mana Web's handler reads the recorded snapshot (its `rememberLastKnownPermanentCard` record
  is gone). `PerpetuallyGiveLandExtraManaEffectHandler` writes `youTapThisLandForMana()`.
- The cards write what the handlers judged (`scripts/step15-run17z13e2-cards.py`, 55 card classes): the Auras and
  C.A.M.P. `enchantedLandTappedForMana()`; Savage Firecat, Sasaya's Essence, Forsaken Monument's land trigger, Mirari's
  Wake, Nikya, Vorinclex, Zendikar Resurgent, Caged Sun, Crypt Ghast, Nissa, Nirkana Revenant, Groundchuck & Dirtbag,
  Ultima `youTapLandForMana()`; War's Toll and Mana Web `opponentTapsLandForMana()`; Forbidden Orchard
  `youTapThisLandForMana()`; the subtypes, Gauntlet of Power's basic and Extraplanar Lens's name the `withFilter`; Regal
  Behemoth's monarch `TriggerOptions.DEFAULT.withEventCondition(new ControllerIsMonarch())`; Price of Glory
  `withInterveningIf(new NotCondition(new TargetPlayerTurn()))`; Treasure Nabber
  `opponentTapsPermanentForMana().withFilter(new PermanentIsArtifactPredicate())` with
  `GainControlOfTargetEffect.ofTriggeringPermanent` (new component: "that artifact", no target: the default chooses a
  targeted effect's target); War's Toll's "tap all lands that player controls" `TapPermanentsEffect(ALL_PERMANENTS,
  land + PermanentControlledByTriggeringPlayerPredicate)` (it was `TARGET_PLAYERS_PERMANENTS`, a player target the old
  handler filled; `TapPermanentsEffectHandler`'s all-permanents filter now reads the triggering player); Rainbow Vale one
  mana ability `[AwardAnyColorManaEffect, RegisterDelayedChooseOpponentGainsControlOfSourceEffect]`, the second resolved
  by the new `RegisterDelayedChooseOpponentGainsControlOfSourceManaAbilityEffectHandler`; The Temporal Anchor
  `withEventCondition(new EventValueAtLeast(1))`.
- The untap-step watch's handler is its default (`MiscTriggerCollectorService.handleUntapStepDefault`): the count as
  event value and the source snapshot whatever the effects are.
- The library defaults: `DiscardTriggerCollectorService.handleCycleDefault` ("whenever a player cycles a card": cycling
  discards the card, CR 702.29a, so `recordDiscard` records the cycling player and the cycled card with its stay); the
  discard, cycling, discard-event, "you cycle" and opponent-caused defaults share one path that routes a permanent or
  player target to `DiscardControllerTriggerTarget`, which now carries the discard (`withDiscard`: the player, the cards
  and their stays; three new components) into the entry it makes (`PermanentChoiceTriggerHandlerService` and the
  optional no-target push record it, without a "that player" target); 10 discard handlers gone. The scry default
  records the scrying player always and its targeted branch carries the player and the count (`withTriggeringPlayer`,
  `withEventValue`); the scry watch judge gives the count as the event's value; 2 handlers gone. The surveil default
  records the player and the source snapshot and routes a "whenever you surveil" target to its choice (an opponent's
  surveil keeps "that player" as its non-targeting target: River Song); its counters handler is gone.
- `step15-run17z13e-audit.py`: `DONE_ROWS` (17z13e2, 17z13e6) and the summary's "done row" lines; the 17z6 and 17z11
  audits' notes. `agent-docs` follow (`scripts/step15-run17z13e2-docs.py`; `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s trigger-state note by

Firecat, Groundchuck & Dirtbag, Ultima, Caged Sun, Gauntlet of Power, Extraplanar Lens, Regal Behemoth, Mana Web, War's

**Rules fixes.**

- Rainbow Vale's control change belongs to its own mana ability: tapped for {B} through Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth's
  Swamp ability it went to the opponent. `RainbowValeTest.anotherManaAbilityGivesNoControlChange` fails at HEAD (the land went to the opponent at the end
  step) and passes.
- Caged Sun's extra mana for a land that left as its mana ability resolved (Gemstone Mine's last use, green chosen) was
  lost: the handler looked for the land on the battlefield; the effect reads it as it last existed.
  `CagedSunTest.departedLandsManaGetsBonus` fails at HEAD (1 green mana, expected 2) and passes.

**Behaviour changes, not rules fixes.** An effect of a cycling, permanent-for-mana or creature-for-mana ability that no
handler named now triggers (no card had one). A cycling entry has the cycling player as its non-targeting "that
player". "Add" goes to the ability's controller and "its controller adds" to the land's controller, not to the tapper
(the same player but under Piracy, where the Aura, Vernal Bloom and Snowfall cases kept their results). Price of Glory's
intervening "if" is checked again as it resolves (the same turn). Treasure Nabber's and War's Toll's effects target
nothing, as before, through their effects.

**Not changed, noted.**

- Extraplanar Lens's "its controller adds" still goes to the tapper (the `AddOneOfEach…` handler's recipient): the same
  player but under Piracy. Mana Web's "a land an opponent controls" is judged by the tapping player, as before.
- `AddManaWhenLandOfColorTappedForManaEffect` adds {C} for a land that could produce it even when the tap reported
  another color (its handler moved as it was; CR 106.12a reads "produces the specified type").
- A targeted untap-step ability would go on the stack with no target (no card has one). A targeted scry ability's
  choice carries no cards-looked-at count (no card reads both).
- `DiscardControllerTriggerTarget`'s new components are immutable (`List.copyOf`, `Map.copyOf`), shared by a simulation
  copy as the record is; no `GameData`, `StackEntry`, `Permanent` or `Card` state is new.

#### Run 17z13e9: the permanent-damage watches have one default each, and the combat damage step uses it (row 17z13e9)

**What the reading found** (each handler of `step15-run17z13e-audit.py --watch DamageWatch` and `--watch CombatWatch`
and `CombatDamageService.processDealtDamageTriggers` read, the cards found by a grep of their triggers and read against
their Oracle text):

- "Whenever this is dealt damage" (`ON_DEALT_DAMAGE`, and `ON_NONCOMBAT_DAMAGE_TO_SELF`, whose default only called the
  other's) had a default whose plain entry recorded the damage, the source and its controller and the damaged
  permanent's snapshot, but whose targeted branch recorded the damage as X only (no source, no snapshot); two class-keyed
  target routes, `DealDamageToTargetPlayerOrPlaneswalkerEffect` (building the "target opponent or planeswalker" filter
  for the `OPPONENT` relation) and `DealDamageToAnyTargetEffect`, recorded the snapshot but no source; High Priest of
  Penance's `MayEffect` route recorded neither, nor the damage; Archfiend of Spite's "a source an opponent controls" was
  judged by its effect's class (`DamageSourceControllerLosesLifeUnlessSacrificesPermanentsEffect`).
- `CombatDamageService.processDealtDamageTriggers` read the same abilities for combat damage with branches of its own
  keyed by the same two classes (and a generic one), recording the snapshot only on those two, the source only for
  "once for each source" abilities, never judging Archfiend's condition, and putting the entries on the stack outside
  the collectors' dispatch: an effect that makes a triggered ability trigger an additional time (Roaming Throne) didn't
  apply to combat damage. (The noncombat entries' bare `stack.add` did get the copies: `GameData`'s stack list adds them.)
- "Whenever a permanent you control is dealt damage" (`ON_ANY_PERMANENT_DEALT_DAMAGE`) had no default: the Wrathful pair
  and Howlpack Avenger reached the stack through the `DealDamageToAnyTargetEffect` handler (which judged "you control"),
  Donna Noble through the `DealDamageToPlayersEffect` one, which also required `TARGET_PLAYER`; any other effect didn't
  trigger.
- "Whenever a source you control deals noncombat damage to a creature" had no default: Taii Wakeen's "equal to that
  creature's toughness" was judged by its `DrawCardEffect` handler; Crude Abattoir's ability arrived as the
  `ConditionalEffect` the reader wraps its intervening "if" in, with a handler of its own (and a third for its bare
  effect); none recorded the creature.
- "Whenever a creature is dealt damage": the `MayEffect` handler did what the default does (ROUTE); the default sent a
  targeted `MayEffect` to its target choice and every other effect to the stack with the creature as its non-targeting
  `targetId`, which Death Pits of Rath's `DestroyTargetPermanentEffect` and Rite of Passage's
  `PutCounterOnTargetPermanentEffect` used as "it": the class decided what targets.
- Rankle and Torbran's modal chosen at trigger time had a handler of its own; the modal choice carries no damage (no mode
  reads it).

**What changed.**

- `DamageTriggerCollectorService.handleDealtDamageDefault` is the default of both "is dealt damage" watches: the
  damaged permanent's ability (CR 113.7) records the damage as event value, the source of the damage as its triggering
  permanent with that source's controller as it dealt the damage, and the damaged permanent's last known information
  with its damage keywords as its source snapshot (CR 608.2h), whatever the effects are; a targeted ability goes to
  `SpellTargetTriggerAnyTarget` with the same record (the damage as X and event value, the source, its controller, the
  snapshot; CR 603.3d). Its filter is the card's declared one, else the effect's triggered filter, else, for an effect
  whose player half is "target opponent" (`targetPlayerRelation()`), the opponents and the effect's permanent half: the
  filter the class-keyed route built, now built from the relation for any of the collector's triggered abilities with no
  declared target. No damage, no trigger (CR 120.8).
- `TriggerCollectionService.collectDealtDamageAbilities` is the one "is dealt damage" collection: the limit, the
  intervening "if" and the event condition judged as the damage is dealt (CR 603.4) with the damage as the event's value,
  the source as the triggering permanent and its controller as "that player", then the dispatch. The noncombat collector
  and `CombatDamageService.processDealtDamageTriggers` call it; the combat one passes the damaged permanent's last known
  information (`TriggerContext.DamageToCreature.damagedLastKnown`, new) since its creatures may have died, and a combined
  event of several sources names none of them (`collectDealtDamageTriggerData`, CR 603.2c). The combat reader's two
  class-keyed branches and its generic branch are gone.
- "Whenever a permanent you control is dealt damage": `handleAnyPermanentDealtDamageDefault` records the damaged
  permanent (its controller, power and last known information) and the damage whatever the effects are; a targeted
  ability goes to its choice with the same record. The collector judges "you control" (`checkAnyPermanentDealtDamageTriggers`).
- "Whenever a source you control deals noncombat damage to a creature":
  `handleAllySourceDealsNoncombatDamageToCreatureDefault` records the creature, its controller and last known
  information, the damage and the source's snapshot; the collector checks the damaged permanent is a creature and judges
  the abilities with the damage and the creature (`checkAllySourceDealtNoncombatDamageToCreatureTriggers`).
- "Whenever a creature is dealt damage": `handleAnyCreatureDealtDamageDefault` sends every targeted ability, "you may" or
  not, to its choice with the creature as triggering permanent, its controller and the damage (CR 603.3d, 603.5), and
  every other to the stack (`enqueueTrigger`) with the same record, the creature's last known information and the source
  snapshot.
- The self-combat default (`handleSelfDealsCombatDamage`) queues a trigger-time modal's mode choice (CR 603.3c), as every
  other reader routes `ChooseOneAtTriggerTimeEffect`.
- `PermanentChoiceContext.SpellTargetTriggerAnyTarget.triggeringPermanentControllerId` (new component,
  `withTriggeringPermanentController`; the land-tap default passes its entry's): the entry it makes carries it, and the
  entries it makes without a target or with a random one now carry its triggering permanent too.
- The cards (`scripts/step15-run17z13e9-cards.py`): Archfiend of Spite `TriggerOptions.EACH_SOURCE.withEventCondition(new
  NotCondition(new TargetPlayerIsController()))`; Taii Wakeen `TriggerOptions.DEFAULT.withEventCondition(new
  TriggeringPermanentToughnessEqualsEventValue())` (new condition: the triggering permanent's toughness equals the event's
  value); Death Pits of Rath `DestroyReferencedPermanentEffect(PermanentReference.TRIGGERING, true)`, Rite of Passage
  `PutCounterOnReferencedPermanentEffect(PermanentReference.TRIGGERING, CounterType.PLUS_ONE_PLUS_ONE)`.
- 11 class-keyed registrations gone (`scripts/step15-run17z13e9-handlers.py`, with the damage collector's remaining
  banner comments): the row's 8 not ROUTE and its 3 ROUTE (Archfiend's, High Priest's and "a creature is dealt damage"'s
  `MayEffect`), with `ON_NONCOMBAT_DAMAGE_TO_SELF`'s forwarding default (its watch is an annotation of the default now).
- `step15-run17z13e-audit.py`: `DONE_ROWS` adds 17z13e9; the 17z6 and 17z11 audits' notes. `agent-docs` follow
  (`scripts/step15-run17z13e9-docs.py`; `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s damage-to-a-permanent note by hand).

(the combat damage step put the ability on the stack outside the dispatch that counts additional triggers).

snapshot the noncombat one does (Archfiend's "an opponent controls" is judged in combat too; no ordinary combat has a
creature deal combat damage to one its own controller controls), and its entry records the source when one source dealt

global ability its own collector reads (`collectTemporaryGlobalTriggers`, the creature as non-targeting `targetId`),

or triggering player on any watch (no mode of Rankle and Torbran reads one); a row that needs it adds it to the modal
chain for every reader. The "is dealt damage" event condition's "that player" is the source's controller only as the
ability triggers (an event condition is not checked again; no card's intervening "if" names that player). A source with
no controller would pass Archfiend's condition (none deals damage). `processCombatDamageReceivedTriggers` ("whenever this
is dealt combat damage") keeps its own reader (no class key).

**Rules fix.** Roaming Throne didn't make a chosen-type creature's "whenever this creature or another creature you
control dies" trigger an additional time: the collector counted only the creature-death doublers.
`RoamingThroneTest.doublesAllyCreatureDeathTrigger` (Zulaport Cutthroat, a Human, as Grizzly Bears dies to Shock) fails
at HEAD (one Zulaport entry, expected two) and passes.

**Behaviour changes, not rules fixes.**

- A death, leave or own-zone-change ability triggers whatever its effect: an Equipment's delayed return or perpetual
  grant for a token that died (it returns or grants nothing), Tyrannical Pitlord's and Dance of Many's "sacrifice /
  exile the linked permanent" when none is linked, Laquatus's Champion's and Soul Scourge's "that player gains life"
  without a remembered player; each resolves doing nothing (none has an intervening "if", CR 603.4).
- Every creature-death entry records the full death (the `OPPONENT` entry's power as event value, the `EQUIPPED`
  entry's snapshot, the `ALLY` entry's controller, toughness and mana value); "that card" of a copy that died is the
  physical card. A "you may" of these watches is a plain entry with its source permanent id and snapshot instead of
  `queueMayAbility`'s. A "choose one" leaves-the-battlefield or own-arrival ability chooses its mode as it triggers (no
  card has one); an own ability of several effects gets the single-effect record.
- Lifeline's "if" is the ability's intervening "if": checked as it triggers (looking back at the creatures that died
  with it, as before) and again as it resolves through the `ConditionalEffect`, not in the effect's handler.
- Reveillark's graveyard choice begins as the self-trigger target queue is processed, as every other targeted
  leaves-the-battlefield ability's, not while the ability is collected.

**Not changed, noted.** The `ANY_NONTOKEN` and `ENCHANTED_PLAYER_NONTOKEN` defaults keep their records (no class-keyed
handler; "a nontoken creature dies" records no dying permanent). `DeathTriggerTarget` carries no toughness or mana
value (no targeted death ability reads them). The trigger-time modal choice carries no triggering card (no mode reads
one). The artifact-or-creature, graveyard-zone, haunted and damaged-creature collectors are unchanged.

**Behaviour changes, not rules fixes.** Every untargeted draw entry records the drawing player as non-targeting "that
player" and triggering player and its source's snapshot (the `targetId` was targeted before: a "change the target"
effect could have treated the drawing player as a target); the "you may" entries have the reader's description, log

**The step readers' grouping (row 17z13e8c).** The done condition of step 15 is that one triggered ability is one stack
object of its declared effects. Read against it, `StepTriggerService`'s readers each group their own way, by the
effects' target kinds rather than by ability:

- the your-upkeep reader: untargeted effects one entry each (one ability split); "any target" takes every upkeep effect
  of the permanent into one `UpkeepAnyTargetTrigger`, and every player-target effect of the permanent goes into one
  `UpkeepPlayerTargetTrigger` with the first granted ability's target filter (separate abilities merged); a graveyard
  target's ability is read whole (run 17z13e8). The command-zone, graveyard, each-upkeep and opponent- and
  chosen-player-upkeep readers, the draw-step readers and the end-step readers put one entry or target choice per
  effect (but for the end-step multi-target walker);
- the precombat-main reader groups its untargeted effects by ability, but merges each target kind's effects across
  abilities; the postcombat and second-main reader merges by target kind; the beginning-of-combat reader merges every
  ability of the permanent, printed and statically granted, into one entry or one target choice but its untargeted
  "you may"s and modals; the end-of-combat reader merges every ability of the permanent into one entry. The emblem step
  reader alone reads abilities whole.

The cards were written to the readers: 56 cards write two or more abilities on one step trigger (by a scan of their
`addTrigger` calls: beginning of combat 38, upkeep 11, end step 5, precombat main 1, end of combat 1), most of them one
Oracle ability split into several `addTrigger` calls that a merging reader joins again (Reckless Stormseeker's "gets
+1/+0 and gains haste", Bolg's two sentences, Mindwrack Harpy, Harried Dronesmith, Bloodgift Demon's "draws a card and
loses 1 life", Kjeldoran Home Guard), some separate abilities (Corrosion, Tangle Wire, Tetravus, Dawn of the Dead,
Bloodhall Ooze, Palace Siege, Warlock Class, Barrensteppe Siege, Lunar Convocation, Keeper of the Accord); six step
abilities have two effects (Alacrian Armory, Does Machines, Hadana's Climb, Abstract Paintmage, Sanctum of Stone Fangs,
Smile at Death), read whole by their readers today; the grants' abilities (`new TriggeredAbility(Triggers.…)`) aren't
in the count. Two probes confirm the violation through the engine (`scripts/step15-run17z13e8b-probes.py`, applied,
run and reverted; both fail at `e7301f7e84` and after this run):

- `PlaneMergeElfTest.landshipIsOneStackObject`: Plane-Merge Elf's one Landship ability, written as two `addTrigger`
  calls (its look, and "if it's a land, you may reveal it"), is two upkeep stack objects (expected 1, was 2): an
  opponent can respond between them, against CR 603.3.
- `CustodyBattleTest.grantedAndPrintedUpkeepAbilitiesAreSeparate`: Bloodgift Demon's printed "target player draws a card
  and loses 1 life" and Custody Battle's granted "target opponent gains control of this creature unless you sacrifice
  a land" become one stack object with one target chosen through Custody Battle's "target opponent" filter (expected 2,
  was 1): the controller can't order them (CR 603.3b) and the Demon can't target its controller.

The fix is neither a reader nor a card change alone: every step reader has to read `StepAbilityReader.effectsByAbility`
and route each ability whole (its own target choice, its own entry), and the cards that split one ability (each read
against its Oracle text) have to become one ability by script in the same run, or the readers' merge-dependent cards
break. It is every step reader of a 6,500-line service, their target-choice contexts (which take the permanent's effects, not
an ability's) and 56-plus cards; row 17z13e8c holds it with the probes as its rules-fix tests.

  `staticGrantedReads`, `graveyardReads`) and routes each ability whole: a targeted one goes to its target choice
  with all its effects by the kinds they target (CR 603.3d), its own target filter (a granted ability's, Custody
  Battle's "target opponent") over the card's; an untargeted one goes on the stack as written with the reader's record
  (the source snapshot, the attached and granting permanents, "that player", the graveyard stay), a "you may" asked as
  it resolves (CR 603.5), an intervening "if" still wrapped (CR 603.4). The your-upkeep and your-end-step readers route
  through `queueYourUpkeepAbility` and `queueControllerEndStepAbility`, the beginning-of-combat reader through
  `queueBeginningOfCombatAbility`; a modal ability is its "choose one" alone (`modalOf`, which fails loudly on a modal
  written beside other effects); the copy and Capricious Efreet choices, which take one effect, fail loudly on an
  ability of more. The each-precombat-main and end-of-combat readers put one entry per ability; the precombat-main
  reader keeps putting its untargeted abilities on the stack in reverse order (the first resolves first); the
  your-end-step reader's walker for an ability of several target groups (Betor) is per ability. The
  beginning-of-combat reader's untargeted "you may" branch (`queueMayAbility`), its dead targeted-modal branch and its

- Cards (`scripts/step15-run17z13e8c-cards.py`, 43 classes in 20 letter modules): one `addTrigger` of every effect,
  in order; a chained `target(…).addTrigger(…)` keeps its group for every effect; Boros Battleshaper and Betor, an

```
Implement step <N> of effect-slot-refactor.md. First read the whole file (Why, Design, Ground

and why. Don't commit until I say so.
```
